title.raw: 卷22 志第17 五行上 Volume 22 Treatises 17: Five Elements 1

sentences.zh: 《易》以八卦定吉凶，則庖犧所以稱聖也。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes uses the eight trigrams to determine fortune and misfortune; thus is why Fuxi is called a sage.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes uses the eight trigrams to determine good and ill fortune—this is why Fuxi earned the title of sage.

sentences.zh: 《書》以九疇論休咎，則大禹所以為明也。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents uses the nine divisions to discuss prosperity and disaster; thus is why Yu the Great is considered enlightened.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents discusses prosperity and disaster through the nine divisions—this is how Yu the Great came to be renowned for his wisdom.

sentences.zh: 《春秋》以災祥驗行事，則仲尼所以垂法也。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals uses calamities and auspicious signs to verify conduct; thus is why Confucius established his law.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals tests actions against calamities and auspicious signs—this is how Confucius bequeathed his standard to posterity.

sentences.zh: 天道以星象示廢興，則甘、石所以先知也。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven uses stellar phenomena to show rise and fall; thus is why Gan and Shi were able to foreknow.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way reveals the rise and fall of dynasties through the stars—this is how Gan De and Shi Shen gained their reputation for foresight.

sentences.zh: 是以祥符之兆可得而言，妖訛之占所以征驗。

translations.literal: Therefore the portents of auspicious tokens can be discussed, and the divinations of strange disturbances can thus be verified.
translations.idiomatic: Auspicious portents can be described and interpreted, and omens of strange disturbances can be tested against events.

sentences.zh: 夫神則陰陽不測，天則欲人遷善，均乎影響，殊致同歸。

translations.literal: As for the divine, yin and yang are unfathomable; Heaven desires that people turn toward goodness—alike in effect as shadow and echo, different in origin yet converging in outcome.
translations.idiomatic: The divine works through yin and yang in unfathomable ways; Heaven seeks to move people toward goodness. Though the means differ, the effect is as sure as shadow follows form and echo follows sound.

sentences.zh: 漢時有伏生、董仲舒、京房、劉向之倫，能言災異，顧盼六經，有足觀者。

translations.literal: In Han times there were Fu Sheng, Dong Zhongshu, Jing Fang, Liu Xiang, and their kind, who could speak of calamities and anomalies, with reference to the Six Classics—well worth study.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times, scholars such as Fu Sheng, Dong Zhongshu, Jing Fang, and Liu Xiang could discourse on calamities and portents with constant reference to the Six Classics—works well worth reading.

sentences.zh: 劉向曰：「君道得則和氣應，休征生。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: "When the Way of the ruler is correct, harmonious qi responds, and auspicious signs arise.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang said: "When a ruler's conduct accords with the Way, harmonious qi responds and auspicious signs appear.

sentences.zh: 君道違則乖氣應，咎徵發。

translations.literal: When the Way of the ruler deviates, discordant qi responds, and baleful signs manifest.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler's conduct strays from the Way, discordant qi responds and baleful signs emerge.

sentences.zh: 」夫天有七曜，地有五行。

translations.literal: " Heaven has the seven luminaries; Earth has the five phases.
translations.idiomatic: " Heaven holds the seven luminaries; Earth holds the five phases.

sentences.zh: 五事愆違則天地見異，況於日月星辰乎？

translations.literal: When the five affairs transgress and deviate, Heaven and Earth display anomalies—how much more so the sun, moon, and stars?
translations.idiomatic: When the five fundamental duties are violated, Heaven and Earth manifest anomalies—how much more so for the sun, moon, and stars?

sentences.zh: 況于水火金木土乎？

translations.literal: How much more so for water, fire, metal, wood, and earth?
translations.idiomatic: How much more so for water, fire, metal, wood, and earth?

sentences.zh: 若梁武之降號伽藍，齊文宣之盤游市里，陳則蔣山之鳥呼曰「奈何」，周則陽武之魚集空而鬥，隋則鵲巢黼帳，火炎門闕，豈唯天道，亦曰人妖，則祥眚呈形，於何不至？

translations.literal: Consider Liang Wudi taking the religious name of a Buddhist monastery, Northern Qi Wenxuan wandering through the marketplaces; in Chen, birds on Mount Jiang cried "What to do?"; in Zhou, fish at Yangwu gathered in empty space to fight; in Sui, magpies nested in imperial robes and fire blazed at the palace gates—is this not only Heaven's way but also human portents? When auspicious and baleful signs take form, where would they not appear?
translations.idiomatic: Liang Wudi took a monastic religious name; Northern Qi Wenxuan caroused through city streets; in Chen, birds on Mount Jiang cried "What can be done?"; in Northern Zhou, fish at Yangwu gathered in midair to fight; in Sui, magpies nested in imperial embroidered hangings and fire consumed the palace gates. Were these omens from Heaven alone—or also warnings born of human folly? When auspicious and baleful signs take visible form, what realm could escape their reach?

sentences.zh: 亦有脫略政教，張羅樽糈，崇信巫史，重增愆罰。

translations.literal: There are also those who neglect government and education, spread nets for sacrificial offerings, honor shamans and record-keepers, and double punishments for offenses.
translations.idiomatic: Some rulers neglect governance and ritual teaching, lavish resources on sacrificial display, place their faith in shamans and spirit-mediums, and multiply punishments for transgressions.

sentences.zh: 昔懷王事神而秦兵逾進，萇弘尚鬼而諸侯不來。

translations.literal: Formerly King Huai of Chu served the spirits yet Qin troops pressed ever forward; Chang Hong honored ghosts yet the feudal lords would not come.
translations.idiomatic: King Huai of Chu devoted himself to the spirits, yet Qin's armies pressed ever closer; Chang Hong courted the dead, yet the feudal lords refused to rally.

sentences.zh: 性者，生之靜也。

translations.literal: Nature is the stillness of life.
translations.idiomatic: Nature is the innate stillness of living being.

sentences.zh: 欲者，心之使也。

translations.literal: Desire is what the heart sends forth.
translations.idiomatic: Desire is what the heart commands.

sentences.zh: 置情攸往，引類同歸。

translations.literal: Setting sentiment on what is to come, it draws its kind together to the same destination.
translations.idiomatic: When the heart sets its feelings on what lies ahead, like attracts like and all converge on the same outcome.

sentences.zh: 雀乳於空城之側，鷮飛於鼎耳之上。

translations.literal: Sparrows nest beside deserted cities; pheasants fly upon cauldron ears.
translations.idiomatic: Sparrows breed beside empty ramparts; pheasants alight on cauldron handles.

sentences.zh: 短長之制，既曰由人；

translations.literal: The measure of short and long has already been said to depend on people;
translations.idiomatic: Whether life is cut short or prolonged—it is said to depend on human conduct;

sentences.zh: 黔隧崇山，同車共軫。

translations.literal: Dark tunnels and lofty mountains—they ride the same cart with shared axles.
translations.idiomatic: yet whether one travels through dark tunnels or over lofty mountains, all share the same carriage on the same axle.

sentences.zh: 必有神道，裁成倚伏。

translations.literal: There must be a divine way that trims and completes, with reliance and reversal.
translations.idiomatic: Surely there is a divine order that shapes events, where fortune and misfortune alternate.

sentences.zh: 一則以為殃釁，一則以為休征。

translations.literal: One takes them as signs of calamity and offense; another takes them as auspicious portents.
translations.idiomatic: Some read such signs as omens of disaster; others read them as signs of good fortune.

sentences.zh: 故曰德勝不祥而義厭不惠。

translations.literal: Hence it is said: virtue overcomes inauspicious signs, and righteousness repels what is unkind.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the saying: virtue can overcome ill omens, and righteousness can dispel misfortune.

sentences.zh: 是以聖王常由德義，消伏災咎也。

translations.literal: Therefore sage kings constantly rely on virtue and righteousness to quell and subdue calamities and disasters.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason, sage kings consistently cultivate virtue and righteousness to avert and overcome calamities.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「木者東方，威儀容貌也。

translations.literal: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Wood belongs to the East—it is dignity, bearing, and appearance.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Wood corresponds to the East—it governs dignity, bearing, and outward appearance.

sentences.zh: 古者聖王垂則，天子穆穆，諸侯皇皇。

translations.literal: In antiquity sage kings established norms: the Son of Heaven was solemn and dignified; the feudal lords were imposing and stately.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, sage kings established standards of conduct: the Son of Heaven was solemn and dignified, the feudal lords imposing and stately.

sentences.zh: 登輿則有鸞和之節，降車則有佩玉之度，田狩則有三驅之制，飲食則有享獻之禮。

translations.literal: When mounting the carriage there were regulations for bells and harmonics; when dismounting there were standards for jade pendants; on hunting expeditions there was the rule of three-sided drives; at meals there were rites of offering and presentation.
translations.idiomatic: When mounting a carriage, there were regulations governing bells and harmonics; when dismounting, standards for jade pendants; on hunting expeditions, the rule of the three-sided drive; at meals, rites of offering and presentation.

sentences.zh: 無事不出境。

translations.literal: Without pressing business, one did not cross the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Without urgent business, one did not cross the borders.

sentences.zh: 此容貌動作之得節，所以順木氣也。

translations.literal: This propriety in bearing and conduct was how one accorded with the qi of wood.
translations.idiomatic: Such propriety in bearing and conduct was how one accorded with the qi of wood.

sentences.zh: 如人君違時令，失威儀，田獵馳騁，不反宮室，飲食沉湎，不顧禮制，縱欲恣睢，出入無度，多徭役以奪人時，增賦稅以奪人財，則木不曲直。

translations.literal: If the ruler violates the seasons, loses dignity and bearing, hunts and gallops without returning to the palace, indulges in food and drink heedless of ritual propriety, follows desires wantonly without restraint in comings and goings, levies many corvée duties to steal people's time, and increases taxes to steal people's wealth—then wood loses its quality of straightness and suppleness.
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler violates the seasons, abandons dignity and proper bearing, hunts and gallops without returning to the palace, indulges in food and drink heedless of ritual, gives free rein to desire without restraint in comings and goings, levies excessive corvée labor that steals the people's time, and raises taxes that steals their wealth—then wood loses its quality of straightness and suppleness.

sentences.zh: 齊後主，鄴城東青桐樹，有如人狀。

translations.literal: Under Northern Qi Houzhu, an green paulownia tree east of Ye City took a shape like a human being.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Qi Houzhu, a green paulownia tree east of Ye City assumed a human shape.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「王德衰，下人將起，則有木生為人狀。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When royal virtue declines and the lower orders are about to rise up, wood will grow into human form.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When royal virtue declines and the common people are about to rise up, wood will grow into human form.

sentences.zh: 」是時後主怠于國政，耽荒酒色，威儀不肅，馳騁無度，大發徭役，盛修宮室，後二歲而亡。

translations.literal: " At that time Houzhu was negligent in state affairs, indulged in wine and women, lacked dignity and bearing, galloped without restraint, levied corvée on a vast scale, and lavishly built palaces; two years later the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Houzhu neglected state affairs, indulged in wine and women, abandoned dignity and proper bearing, galloped without restraint, levied corvée on a vast scale, and lavishly built palaces. Two years later the state perished.

sentences.zh: 木不曲直之效也。

translations.literal: This was the effect of wood losing its straightness and suppleness.
translations.idiomatic: This was the manifestation of wood losing its quality of straightness and suppleness.

sentences.zh: 七年，宮中有樹，大數圍，夜半無故自拔。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, a tree in the palace, several arm-spans in girth, uprooted itself without cause at midnight.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, a tree in the palace—several arm-spans in girth—uprooted itself without cause at midnight.

sentences.zh: 齊以木德王，無故自拔，亡國之應也。

translations.literal: Qi ruled by the virtue of wood; uprooting itself without cause was the response foretelling the state's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Qi ruled by the virtue of wood; a tree uprooting itself without cause was an omen foretelling the state's destruction.

sentences.zh: 其年，齊亡。

translations.literal: That year, Qi perished.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, Qi fell.

sentences.zh: 四月，幽州人家以白楊木懸灶上，積十餘年，忽生三條，皆長三尺餘，甚鮮茂。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, a household in You Province had white poplar wood hung above the stove; after more than ten years, three shoots suddenly sprouted, each over three feet long and very lush.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, a household in You Province had white poplar wood hung above the stove; after more than ten years, three shoots suddenly sprouted, each over three feet long and remarkably lush.

sentences.zh: 仁壽二年春，盩厔人以楊木為屋樑，生三條，長二尺。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year of Renshou, a person in Zhouzhi used poplar wood as a roof beam; three shoots sprouted, each two feet long.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Renshou, a person in Zhouzhi used poplar wood as a roof beam; three shoots sprouted from it, each two feet long.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「妃後有顓，木僕反立，斷枯複生。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the consort and empress are willful, wood servants stand upright again, and severed dead wood comes back to life.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the empress and consorts are willful and overbearing, severed dead wood stands upright again and sprouts anew.

sentences.zh: 」獨孤後專恣之應也。

translations.literal: " This was the response to Empress Dugu's willful domination.
translations.idiomatic: " This was the omen corresponding to Empress Dugu's willful domination.

sentences.zh: 十月，蘭州楊樹上松生，高三尺，六節十二枝，《宋志》曰：「松不改柯易葉，楊者危脆之木，此永久之業，將集危亡之地也。

translations.literal: In the tenth month, pine grew on a poplar tree in Lanzhou, three feet high with six nodes and twelve branches. The Song Annals says: "Pine does not change its trunk or alter its leaves; poplar is a fragile, brittle wood—this enduring enterprise is about to gather in a place of peril and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month, pine grew on a poplar tree in Lanzhou, three feet high with six nodes and twelve branches. The Song Annals says: "Pine does not change its trunk or alter its leaves; poplar is a fragile, brittle wood—this enduring enterprise is about to settle in a place of peril and destruction.

sentences.zh: 」是時帝惑讒言，幽廢塚嫡，初立晉王為皇太子。

translations.literal: " At that time the emperor was swayed by slander, secretly deposed the heir of the main line, and first installed the Prince of Jin as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the emperor was swayed by slander, secretly deposed the legitimate heir, and installed the Prince of Jin as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，皇太子不勝任，永久之業，將致危亡。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: the crown prince is unfit; the enduring enterprise will lead to peril and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: the crown prince is unfit for his role; the enduring enterprise will lead to peril and destruction.

sentences.zh: 帝不悟。

translations.literal: The emperor did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed the warning.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，太子立，是為煬帝，竟以亡國。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, the crown prince ascended—this was Emperor Yang—and in the end the state was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the crown prince ascended the throne as Emperor Yang, and in the end the state was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 八月，河間柳樹無故枯落，既而花葉複生。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, willow trees in Hejian withered and shed their leaves without cause, then afterward blossoms and leaves grew again.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, willow trees in Hejian withered and shed their leaves without cause, then afterward blossoms and leaves sprouted again.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「木再榮，國有大喪。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When wood flourishes a second time, the state will suffer a great mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When wood flourishes a second time, the state will suffer a great bereavement.

sentences.zh: 」是歲，宮車晏駕。

translations.literal: " That year, the imperial carriage halted at dusk—the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: " That year, the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「金者西方，萬物既成，殺氣之始也。

translations.literal: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Metal belongs to the West—when all things are already formed, it is the beginning of killing qi.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Metal corresponds to the West—when all things are fully formed, it marks the beginning of killing qi.

sentences.zh: 古之王者，興師動眾，建立旗鼓，以誅殘賊，禁暴虐，安天下，殺伐必應義，以順金氣。

translations.literal: Ancient kings raised armies and mobilized the masses, established banners and drums, to punish cruel bandits, restrain violence and tyranny, and pacify the realm—killing and attacking must accord with righteousness, to comply with the qi of metal.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient kings raised armies and mobilized the masses, established banners and drums to punish cruel bandits, restrain violence and tyranny, and pacify the realm—killing and warfare must accord with righteousness to comply with the qi of metal.

sentences.zh: 如人君樂侵陵，好攻戰，貪城邑之賂，以輕百姓之命，人皆不安，外內騷動，則金不從革。

translations.literal: If the ruler delights in aggression and encroachment, loves warfare, covets bribes from cities and towns, and lightly regards the lives of the common people so that all are unsettled and turmoil stirs within and without—then metal does not obey the process of transformation.
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler delights in aggression, loves warfare, covets bribes from conquered cities, and lightly regards the lives of the common people so that all are unsettled and turmoil stirs within and without—then metal does not obey the process of transformation.

sentences.zh: 陳五月，東冶鐵鑄，有物赤色，大如鬥，自天墜熔所。

translations.literal: In Chen, in the fifth month, at the Eastern Foundry where iron was cast, a red object the size of a bushel fell from the sky into the smelting site.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen, in the fifth month, at the Eastern Foundry where iron was cast, a red object the size of a bushel fell from the sky into the smelting site.

sentences.zh: 隆隆有聲，鐵飛破屋而四散，燒人家。

translations.literal: With a rumbling sound, molten iron flew forth, breaking through roofs and scattering in all directions, burning people's homes.
translations.idiomatic: With a rumbling sound, molten iron flew forth, breaking through roofs and scattering in all directions, setting people's homes ablaze.

sentences.zh: 時後主與隋雖結和好，遣兵度江，掩襲城鎮，將士勞敝，府藏空竭。

translations.literal: At that time, although Houzhu had made peace with Sui, he sent troops across the river to raid towns; soldiers and officers were exhausted and the treasury was emptied.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, although Houzhu had made peace with Sui, he sent troops across the river to raid towns; soldiers and officers were exhausted and the treasury was depleted.

sentences.zh: 東冶者，陳人鑄兵之所。

translations.literal: The Eastern Foundry was where the people of Chen cast weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Foundry was where the people of Chen cast weapons.

sentences.zh: 鐵飛為變者，金不從革之應。

translations.literal: Molten iron flying forth as a transformation was the response to metal not obeying the process of transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Molten iron flying forth as a transformation was the omen corresponding to metal not obeying the process of transformation.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，陳國小而兵弱，當以和好為固，無鑄兵而黷武，以害百姓。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: Chen is small and its armies weak—it should rely on peace and friendship for security, not cast weapons and abuse warfare to harm the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: Chen is small and its armies weak—it should rely on peace and friendship for security, not cast weapons and abuse warfare to harm the common people.

sentences.zh: 後主不悟，又遣偽將陳紀、任蠻奴、蕭摩訶數寇江北，百姓不堪其役。

translations.literal: Houzhu did not understand, and again sent the false generals Chen Ji, Ren Mannu, and Xiao Mohe to raid north of the river many times; the common people could not bear the burden of service.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu did not heed the warning and again sent the generals Chen Ji, Ren Mannu, and Xiao Mohe to raid north of the river repeatedly; the common people could not bear the burden of service.

sentences.zh: 及隋師渡江，而二將降款，卒以滅亡。

translations.literal: When Sui troops crossed the river, two of the generals surrendered, and in the end the state was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui troops crossed the river, two of the generals surrendered, and in the end the state was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「火者南方，陽光為明也。

translations.literal: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Fire belongs to the South—yang light is its brightness.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Fire corresponds to the South—yang light is its brightness.

sentences.zh: 人君向南，蓋取象也。

translations.literal: The ruler facing south takes this as his symbol.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler facing south takes this as his symbol.

sentences.zh: 昔者聖帝明王，負扆攝袂，南面而聽斷天下。

translations.literal: Formerly sage emperors and enlightened kings, leaning on the screen and gathering their sleeves, faced south to judge and decide the affairs of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, sage emperors and enlightened kings, leaning on the screen and gathering their sleeves, faced south to judge and decide the affairs of the realm.

sentences.zh: 攬海內之雄俊，積之於朝，以續聰明，推邪佞之偽臣，投之於野，以通壅塞，以順火氣。

translations.literal: They gathered the outstanding talents from within the seas and accumulated them at court to extend their clarity and wisdom; they pushed away wicked and sycophantic false ministers and cast them into the wilds to clear blockages—thus complying with the qi of fire.
translations.idiomatic: They gathered outstanding talents from across the realm and accumulated them at court to extend their clarity and wisdom; they cast away wicked and sycophantic ministers into the wilds to clear obstructions—thus complying with the qi of fire.

sentences.zh: 夫不明之君，惑於讒口，白黑雜揉，代相是非，眾邪並進，人君疑惑。

translations.literal: An unenlightened ruler, deluded by slanderous mouths, mixes black and white so that right and wrong alternate in succession; many evils advance together and the ruler is filled with doubt.
translations.idiomatic: An unenlightened ruler, deluded by slander, mingles truth and falsehood so that right and wrong alternate in succession; many evils advance together and the ruler is filled with doubt.

sentences.zh: 棄法律，間骨肉，殺太子，逐功臣，以孽代宗，則火失其性。

translations.literal: Abandoning the laws, estranging kin, killing the crown prince, driving away meritorious ministers, and replacing the legitimate heir with a bastard—then fire loses its nature.
translations.idiomatic: Abandoning the laws, estranging kin, killing the crown prince, driving away meritorious ministers, and replacing the legitimate heir with a bastard—then fire loses its nature.

sentences.zh: 梁五月，有盜入南、北掖，燒神武門總章觀。

translations.literal: In Liang, in the fifth month, thieves entered the Southern and Northern Side Gates and burned the Shenwu Gate and Zongzhang Observatory.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang, in the fifth month, thieves entered the Southern and Northern Side Gates and burned the Shenwu Gate and Zongzhang Observatory.

sentences.zh: 時帝初即位，而火燒觀闕，不祥之甚也。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor had just ascended the throne, and fire burned the observatory towers—an extremely inauspicious sign.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor had just ascended the throne, and fire consumed the observatory towers—an extremely inauspicious sign.

sentences.zh: 既而太子薨，皇孫不得立。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the crown prince died, and the imperial grandson could not be installed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the crown prince died, and the imperial grandson could not be installed as heir.

sentences.zh: 及帝暮年，惑於硃異之口，果有侯景之亂，宮室多被焚燒。

translations.literal: When the emperor reached his later years, deluded by the words of Zhu Yi, the rebellion of Hou Jing indeed arose, and many palace buildings were burned.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor reached his later years, deluded by the words of Zhu Yi, the rebellion of Hou Jing indeed arose, and many palace buildings were burned.

sentences.zh: 天誡所以先見也。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning had thus appeared in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning had thus appeared in advance.

sentences.zh: 五月，琬琰殿火，延燒後宮三千餘間。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Wanyan Hall caught fire, and the blaze spread to more than three thousand rooms of the rear palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the Wanyan Hall caught fire, and the blaze spread to more than three thousand rooms of the rear palace.

sentences.zh: ，朱雀航華表災。

translations.literal: The ornamental column at the Zhuque Bridge was destroyed by disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The ornamental column at the Zhuque Bridge was destroyed by fire.

sentences.zh: 明年，同泰寺災。

translations.literal: The next year, the Tongtai Temple was destroyed by disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, the Tongtai Temple was destroyed by fire.

sentences.zh: ，硃雀門災。

translations.literal: The Zhuque Gate was destroyed by disaster.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhuque Gate was destroyed by fire.

sentences.zh: 水沴火也。

translations.literal: Water harms fire.
translations.idiomatic: Water was harming fire.

sentences.zh: 是時帝崇尚佛道，宗廟牲牷，皆以面代之，又委萬乘之重，數詣同泰寺，捨身為奴，令王公已下贖之。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor revered Buddhism, substituting dough for sacrificial animals at the ancestral temple; he also entrusted the weight of imperial rule, repeatedly going to the Tongtai Temple to offer himself as a slave, ordering princes and officials downward to ransom him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor revered Buddhism, substituting dough for sacrificial animals at the ancestral temple; he also set aside the weight of imperial rule, repeatedly going to the Tongtai Temple to offer himself as a slave, ordering princes and officials downward to ransom him.

sentences.zh: 初陽為不許，後為默許，方始還宮。

translations.literal: At first he openly refused permission; afterward he tacitly permitted it—only then did he return to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At first he openly refused permission; afterward he tacitly permitted it—only then did he return to the palace.

sentences.zh: 天誡若曰，梁武為國主，不遵先王之法，而淫於佛道，橫多糜費，將使其社稷不得血食也。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: Liang Wu as ruler of the state did not follow the laws of former kings but indulged excessively in Buddhism, wantonly wasting resources—it would cause his altars of soil and grain to receive no blood offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: Liang Wu, as ruler of the state, did not follow the laws of former kings but indulged excessively in Buddhism, wantonly wasting resources—it would cause his altars of soil and grain to receive no blood offerings.

sentences.zh: 天數見變而帝不悟，後竟以亡。

translations.literal: Heaven repeatedly displayed transformations yet the emperor did not understand; afterward he perished and the state was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven repeatedly displayed transformations yet the emperor did not heed them; afterward he perished and the state was lost.

sentences.zh: 及江陵之敗，闔城為賤隸焉，即捨身為奴之應也。

translations.literal: When Jiangling fell, the entire city became slaves—this was the response to offering oneself as a slave.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangling fell, the entire city became slaves—this was the omen corresponding to his offering himself as a slave.

sentences.zh: 陳，重雲殿災。

translations.literal: In Chen, the Chongyun Hall was destroyed by disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen, the Chongyun Hall was destroyed by fire.

sentences.zh: 東魏十一月，閶闔門災。

translations.literal: In Eastern Wei, in the eleventh month, the Changhe Gate was destroyed by disaster.
translations.idiomatic: In Eastern Wei, in the eleventh month, the Changhe Gate was destroyed by fire.

sentences.zh: 是時齊神武作宰，而大野拔斬樊子鵠，以州來降，神武聽讒而殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Gao Huan of Qi served as chief minister; Daye Ba beheaded Fan Zihu, who had surrendered with his province, yet Huan listened to slander and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Gao Huan of Qi served as chief minister; Daye Ba beheaded Fan Zihu, who had surrendered with his province, yet Huan listened to slander and killed him.

sentences.zh: 司空元暉免。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Yuan Hui was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Yuan Hui was dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 逐功臣大臣之罰也。

translations.literal: This was the punishment for driving away meritorious ministers and great officials.
translations.idiomatic: This was the punishment for driving away meritorious ministers and great officials.

sentences.zh: 八月，廣宗郡火，燒數千家。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, fire in Guangzong Commandery burned several thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, fire in Guangzong Commandery burned several thousand households.

sentences.zh: 後齊後主，九龍殿災，延燒西廊。

translations.literal: Under Later Qi Houzhu, the Jiulong Hall was destroyed by disaster, and the blaze spread to the western corridor.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi Houzhu, the Jiulong Hall was destroyed by fire, and the blaze spread to the western corridor.

sentences.zh: 四年，昭陽、宣光、瑤華三殿災，延燒龍舟。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, the Zhaoyang, Xuangguang, and Yaohua halls were destroyed by disaster, and the blaze spread to the dragon boat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, the Zhaoyang, Xuangguang, and Yaohua halls were destroyed by fire, and the blaze spread to the dragon boat.

sentences.zh: 是時讒言任用，正士道消，祖孝徵作歌謠，斛律明月以誅死。

translations.literal: At that time slanderous words were employed in office; the way of upright men faded; Zu Xiaozheng composed ballads; Hulü Mingyue was executed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time slanderous advisers were employed in office; the way of upright men faded; Zu Xiaozheng composed ballads; Hulü Mingyue was executed.

sentences.zh: 讒夫昌，邪勝正之應也。

translations.literal: Slanderers flourished—this was the response to evil overcoming righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Slanderers flourished—this was the omen corresponding to evil overcoming righteousness.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「君不思道，厥妖火燒宮。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the ruler does not reflect on the Way, the anomaly is fire burning the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When the ruler does not reflect on the Way, the anomaly is fire burning the palace.

sentences.zh: ，將祠泰山，令使者致石像神祠之所。

translations.literal: About to sacrifice at Mount Tai, he ordered envoys to deliver a stone image to the site of the spirit shrine.
translations.idiomatic: About to sacrifice at Mount Tai, he ordered envoys to deliver a stone image to the site of the spirit shrine.

sentences.zh: 未至數裡，野火欻起，燒像碎如小塊。

translations.literal: Before reaching it by several li, wildfire suddenly arose and burned the image, shattering it into small pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Before reaching it by several li, wildfire suddenly arose and burned the image, shattering it into small pieces.

sentences.zh: 時帝頗信讒言，猜阻骨肉，滕王瓚失志而死，創業功臣，多被夷滅，故天見變，而帝不悟，其後太子勇竟被廢戮。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor largely believed slanderous words, suspected and obstructed his kin; Prince Teng Zan died in despair; many founding meritorious officials were exterminated—therefore Heaven displayed transformations, yet the emperor did not understand; afterward Crown Prince Yong was ultimately deposed and executed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor largely believed slander, suspected and obstructed his kin; Prince Teng Zan died in despair; many founding meritorious officials were exterminated—therefore Heaven displayed transformations, yet the emperor did not heed them; afterward Crown Prince Yong was ultimately deposed and executed.

sentences.zh: ，顯陽門災，舊名廣陽，則帝之姓名也。

translations.literal: The Xianyang Gate was destroyed by fire; its old name was Guangyang—the emperor's personal name.
translations.idiomatic: The Xianyang Gate was destroyed by fire; its old name was Guangyang—the emperor's personal name.

sentences.zh: 國門之崇顯，號令之所由出也。

translations.literal: The majesty of the national gate is where commands issue forth.
translations.idiomatic: The majesty of the national gate is where commands issue forth.

sentences.zh: 時帝不遵法度，驕奢荒怠，裴蘊、虞世基之徒，阿諛順旨，掩塞聰明，宇文述以讒邪顯進，忠諫者鹹被誅戮。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor did not observe laws and regulations, was arrogant, extravagant, and negligent; Pei Yun, Yu Shiji, and their kind flattered and followed his wishes, blocking his clear hearing; Yuwen Shu advanced through slander and wickedness; loyal remonstrators were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor did not observe laws and regulations, was arrogant, extravagant, and negligent; Pei Yun, Yu Shiji, and their kind flattered and followed his wishes, blocking his clear hearing; Yuwen Shu advanced through slander and wickedness; loyal remonstrators were all executed.

sentences.zh: 天戒若曰，信讒害忠，則除「廣陽」也。

translations.literal: Heaven's warning seemed to say: trust slander and harm the loyal—then remove "Guangyang."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's warning seemed to say: trust slander and harm the loyal—then remove "Guangyang."

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「水者，北方之藏，氣至陰也。

translations.literal: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Water is the storehouse of the North—the qi of utmost yin.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Water is the storehouse of the North—the qi of utmost yin.

sentences.zh: 宗廟者，祭祀之象也。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple is the symbol of sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The ancestral temple is the symbol of sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 故天子親耕以供粢盛，王后親蠶以供祭服。

translations.literal: Therefore the Son of Heaven personally plows to supply sacrificial grain, and the queen personally tends silkworms to supply sacrificial garments.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Son of Heaven personally plows to supply sacrificial grain, and the queen personally tends silkworms to supply sacrificial garments.

sentences.zh: 敬之至也。

translations.literal: This is the utmost of reverence.
translations.idiomatic: This is the utmost of reverence.

sentences.zh: 發號施令，十二月鹹得其氣，則水氣順。

translations.literal: When issuing commands and implementing policies, all twelve months obtain their proper qi, then the qi of water is harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: When issuing commands and implementing policies, all twelve months obtain their proper qi, then the qi of water is harmonious.

sentences.zh: 如人君簡宗廟，不禱祀，逆天時，則水不潤下。

translations.literal: If the ruler neglects the ancestral temple, does not pray and sacrifice, and goes against the seasons, then water does not moisten downward.
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler neglects the ancestral temple, does not pray and sacrifice, and goes against the seasons, then water does not moisten downward.

sentences.zh: 梁六月，太末、信安、豐安三縣大水。

translations.literal: In Liang, in the sixth month, Taiwu, Xin'an, and Feng'an commanderies suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang, in the sixth month, Taiwu, Xin'an, and Feng'an commanderies suffered great floods.

sentences.zh: 《春秋考異郵》曰：「陰盛臣逆人悲，則水出河決。

translations.literal: The Spring and Autumn Annals' Investigation of Anomalies says: "When yin flourishes, ministers rebel, and people grieve, then water overflows the river banks.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn Annals' Investigation of Anomalies says: "When yin flourishes, ministers rebel, and people grieve, then water overflows the river banks.

sentences.zh: 」是時江州刺史陳伯之、益州刺史劉季連舉兵反叛，師旅數興，百姓愁怨，臣逆人悲之應也。

translations.literal: " At that time the Inspector of Jiang Province Chen Bozhi and the Inspector of Yi Province Liu Jilian raised armies in rebellion; troops were repeatedly mobilized, the common people were filled with sorrow and resentment—this was the response to ministers rebelling and people grieving.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the Inspector of Jiang Province Chen Bozhi and the Inspector of Yi Province Liu Jilian raised armies in rebellion; troops were repeatedly mobilized, the common people were filled with sorrow and resentment—this was the omen corresponding to ministers rebelling and people grieving.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，建康大水，濤上御道七尺。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, eighth month, Jiankang suffered a great flood; waves rose seven feet above the imperial road.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, eighth month, Jiankang suffered a great flood; waves rose seven feet above the imperial road.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，建康又大水。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, fifth month, Jiankang again suffered a great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, fifth month, Jiankang again suffered a great flood.

sentences.zh: 是時數興師旅，以拒魏軍。

translations.literal: At that time troops were repeatedly mobilized to resist the Wei army.
translations.idiomatic: At that time troops were repeatedly mobilized to resist the Wei army.

sentences.zh: 十二年四月，建康大水。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, fourth month, Jiankang suffered a great flood.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, fourth month, Jiankang suffered a great flood.

sentences.zh: 是時大發卒築浮山堰，以遏淮水，勞役連年，百姓悲怨之應也。

translations.literal: At that time corvée laborers were massively conscripted to build the Floating Mountain Dam to block the Huai River; forced labor continued for years—the common people's sorrow and resentment was the response.
translations.idiomatic: At that time corvée laborers were massively conscripted to build the Floating Mountain Dam to block the Huai River; forced labor continued for years—the common people's sorrow and resentment was the corresponding omen.

sentences.zh: 五月，建康大水，御道通船。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Jiankang suffered a great flood; boats could pass along the imperial road.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Jiankang suffered a great flood; boats could pass along the imperial road.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「大水至國，賤人將貴。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When great floods reach the state, the lowly will become exalted.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When great floods reach the state, the lowly will become exalted.

sentences.zh: 」蕭棟、侯景僭稱尊號之應也。

translations.literal: " This was the response to Xiao Dong and Hou Jing presumptuously assuming imperial titles.
translations.idiomatic: " This was the omen corresponding to Xiao Dong and Hou Jing presumptuously assuming imperial titles.

sentences.zh: 後齊十二月，兗、趙、魏三州大水。

translations.literal: Under Later Qi, in the twelfth month, Yan, Zhao, and Wei provinces suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi, in the twelfth month, Yan, Zhao, and Wei provinces suffered great floods.

sentences.zh: ，并州汾水溢。

translations.literal: The Fen River in Bing Province overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: The Fen River in Bing Province overflowed.

sentences.zh: 京房曰：「水者純陰之精，陰氣洋溢者，小人專制。

translations.literal: Jing Fang said: "Water is the pure essence of yin; when yin qi overflows, petty men hold sole power.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang said: "Water is the pure essence of yin; when yin qi overflows, petty men hold sole power.

sentences.zh: 」是時和士開、元文遙、趙彥深專任之應也。

translations.literal: " At that time He Shikai, Yuan Wenyao, and Zhao Yanshen held sole authority—this was the response.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time He Shikai, Yuan Wenyao, and Zhao Yanshen held sole authority—this was the corresponding omen.

sentences.zh: 八月，山東諸州大水。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the provinces east of the mountains suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, the provinces east of the mountains suffered great floods.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「小人踴躍，無所畏忌，陰不制于陽，則湧水出。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When petty men leap about without fear or restraint, and yin does not restrain yang, then surging water appears.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When petty men leap about without fear or restraint, and yin does not restrain yang, then surging water appears.

sentences.zh: 」是時群小用事，邪佞滿朝。

translations.literal: " At that time petty men held office; the wicked and sycophantic filled the court.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time petty men held office; the wicked and sycophantic filled the court.

sentences.zh: 閹豎嬖幸，伶人封王。

translations.literal: Eunuchs and favorites were ennobled as kings; entertainers were enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs and favorites were ennobled as kings; entertainers were enfeoffed as princes.

sentences.zh: 此其所以應也。

translations.literal: This was why the omen appeared.
translations.idiomatic: This was why the omen appeared.

sentences.zh: ，河南八州大水。

translations.literal: The eight provinces of Henan suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: The eight provinces of Henan suffered great floods.

sentences.zh: 是時獨孤皇后干預政事，濫殺宮人，放黜宰相。

translations.literal: At that time Empress Dugu intervened in government affairs, wantonly killed palace women, and dismissed and banished chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Empress Dugu intervened in government affairs, wantonly killed palace women, and dismissed and banished chancellors.

sentences.zh: 楊素頗專。

translations.literal: Yang Su held considerable sole authority.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su held considerable sole authority.

sentences.zh: 水陰氣，臣妾盛強之應也。

translations.literal: Water is yin qi—this was the response to ministers and consorts growing powerful.
translations.idiomatic: Water is yin qi—this was the omen corresponding to ministers and consorts growing powerful.

sentences.zh: ，河南、河北諸州大水。

translations.literal: The provinces of Henan and Hebei suffered great floods.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces of Henan and Hebei suffered great floods.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「顓事有智，誅罰絕理，則厥災水。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When willful conduct prevails and punishments and executions violate reason, then the calamity is flood.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When willful conduct prevails and punishments and executions violate reason, then the calamity is flood.

sentences.zh: 」亦由帝用刑嚴急，臣下有小過，帝或親臨斬決，又先是柱國史萬歲以忤旨被戮，誅罰絕理之應也。

translations.literal: " This was also because the emperor used punishments with severity and urgency; when subordinates had minor faults, the emperor sometimes personally attended their execution. Earlier, the Pillar of State Shi Wansui had been executed for defying the imperial will—this was the response to punishments and executions violating reason.
translations.idiomatic: " This was also because the emperor used punishments with severity and urgency; when subordinates had minor faults, the emperor sometimes personally attended their execution. Earlier, the Pillar of State Shi Wansui had been executed for defying the imperial will—this was the omen corresponding to punishments and executions violating reason.

sentences.zh: ，河南大水，漂沒三十餘郡。

translations.literal: Henan suffered a great flood that submerged more than thirty commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Henan suffered a great flood that submerged more than thirty commanderies.

sentences.zh: 帝嗣位已來，未親郊廟之禮，簡宗廟，廢祭祀之應也。

translations.literal: Since ascending the throne, the emperor had not personally performed suburban and temple rites—this was the response to neglecting the ancestral temple and abandoning sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Since ascending the throne, the emperor had not personally performed suburban and temple rites—this was the omen corresponding to neglecting the ancestral temple and abandoning sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「土者中央，為內事。

translations.literal: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Earth belongs to the Center—it governs internal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Earth corresponds to the Center—it governs internal affairs.

sentences.zh: 宮室台榭，夫婦親屬也。

translations.literal: Palaces and pavilions represent husband and wife and kin.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces and pavilions represent husband and wife and kin.

sentences.zh: 古者自天子至於士，宮室寢居，大小有差，高卑異等，骨肉有恩。

translations.literal: In antiquity, from the Son of Heaven down to the scholar-official, dwelling places differed in size, height and lowliness had their ranks, and kin had their proper affection.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, from the Son of Heaven down to the scholar-official, dwelling places differed in size, height and lowliness had their ranks, and kin had their proper affection.

sentences.zh: 故明王賢君，修宮室之制，謹夫婦之別，加親戚之思，敬父兄之禮，則中氣和。

translations.literal: Therefore enlightened kings and worthy rulers regulated the system of palaces, maintained the distinction between husband and wife, strengthened affection for kin, and honored the rites due to fathers and elder brothers—then the central qi was harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore enlightened kings and worthy rulers regulated the system of palaces, maintained the distinction between husband and wife, strengthened affection for kin, and honored the rites due to fathers and elder brothers—then the central qi was harmonious.

sentences.zh: 人君肆心縱意，大為宮室，高為台榭，雕文刻鏤，以疲人力，淫泆無別，妻妾過度，犯親戚，侮父兄，中氣亂，則稼穡不成。

translations.literal: If the ruler follows his heart's whims, builds palaces on a vast scale, raises towers and pavilions to great heights, carves and inlays ornamentation to exhaust human labor, indulges in licentiousness without distinction, takes concubines beyond measure, offends kin, and insults fathers and elder brothers—then the central qi is disordered and crops fail.
translations.idiomatic: If a ruler follows his heart's whims, builds palaces on a vast scale, raises towers and pavilions to great heights, carves and inlays ornamentation to exhaust human labor, indulges in licentiousness without distinction, takes concubines beyond measure, offends kin, and insults fathers and elder brothers—then the central qi is disordered and crops fail.

sentences.zh: 齊後主，山東饑。

translations.literal: Under Northern Qi Houzhu, Shandong suffered famine.
translations.idiomatic: Under Northern Qi Houzhu, Shandong suffered famine.

sentences.zh: 是時，大興土木之功于仙都苑。

translations.literal: At that time, massive construction projects were launched at the Xiandu Garden.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, massive construction projects were launched at the Xiandu Garden.

sentences.zh: 又起宮於邯鄲，窮侈極麗。

translations.literal: Palaces were also built at Handan, reaching the utmost of extravagance and splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Palaces were also built at Handan, reaching the utmost of extravagance and splendor.

sentences.zh: 後宮侍御千餘人，皆寶衣玉食。

translations.literal: More than a thousand palace attendants and consorts all wore precious garments and ate jade-like fare.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand palace attendants and consorts all wore precious garments and ate jade-like fare.

sentences.zh: 逆中氣之咎也。

translations.literal: This was the fault of violating the central qi.
translations.idiomatic: This was the fault of violating the central qi.

sentences.zh: 煬帝，燕、代、齊、魯諸郡饑。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Yang, Yan, Dai, Qi, and Lu commanderies suffered famine.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang, Yan, Dai, Qi, and Lu commanderies suffered famine.

sentences.zh: 先是建立東都，制度崇侈。

translations.literal: Earlier, the Eastern Capital had been established with a system of lofty extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the Eastern Capital had been established with a system of lofty extravagance.

sentences.zh: 又宗室諸王，多遠徙邊郡。

translations.literal: Also, many princes of the imperial clan were exiled to distant frontier commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Also, many princes of the imperial clan were exiled to distant frontier commanderies.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「貌之不恭，是謂不肅，則下不敬。

translations.literal: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "When appearance is not reverent, this is called lack of dignity, and subordinates are not respectful.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "When appearance is not reverent, this is called lack of dignity, and subordinates are not respectful.

sentences.zh: 陰氣勝，故厥咎狂，厥罰常雨，厥極惡。

translations.literal: Yin qi prevails; therefore the fault is madness, the punishment is constant rain, and the extreme is evil.
translations.idiomatic: Yin qi prevails; therefore the fault is madness, the punishment is constant rain, and the extreme is evil.

sentences.zh: 時則有服妖，時則有龜孽，有雞禍，有下體生上體之屙，有青眚青祥。

translations.literal: At such times there are clothing anomalies, turtle portents, chicken calamities, discharges where the lower body produces what belongs to the upper body, and green baleful signs and green omens.
translations.idiomatic: At such times there are clothing anomalies, turtle portents, chicken calamities, discharges where the lower body produces what belongs to the upper body, and green baleful signs and green omens.

sentences.zh: 惟金沴木。

translations.literal: Only metal harms wood.
translations.idiomatic: Only metal harms wood.

sentences.zh: ○貌不恭

translations.literal: ○ Irreverent appearance
translations.idiomatic: ○ Irreverent appearance

sentences.zh: 侯景僭即尊號，升圓丘，行不能正履，有識者知其不免。

translations.literal: Hou Jing presumptuously assumed an imperial title, ascended the Round Mound, and could not walk properly when performing the rites—those with insight knew he would not escape destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing presumptuously assumed an imperial title, ascended the Round Mound, and could not walk properly when performing the rites—those with insight knew he would not escape destruction.

sentences.zh: 景尋敗。

translations.literal: Jing was soon defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Jing was soon defeated.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝既平侯景，破蕭紀，而有驕矜之色。

translations.literal: After Liang Yuan Di had pacified Hou Jing and defeated Xiao Ji, he displayed an air of arrogance and self-satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: After Liang Yuan Di had pacified Hou Jing and defeated Xiao Ji, he displayed an air of arrogance and self-satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 性又沉猜，由是臣下離貳。

translations.literal: His nature was also deep and suspicious; because of this, ministers and subordinates became divided and estranged.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was also deep and suspicious; because of this, ministers and subordinates became divided and estranged.

sentences.zh: 既位三年而為西魏所陷，帝竟不得其死。

translations.literal: Three years after taking the throne, he was overrun by Western Wei; the emperor ultimately did not die a natural death.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after taking the throne, he was overrun by Western Wei; the emperor ultimately did not die a natural death.

sentences.zh: 陳後主每祀郊廟，必稱疾不行。

translations.literal: Chen Houzhu, whenever he was to sacrifice at the suburban altars and ancestral temple, invariably claimed illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Houzhu, whenever he was to sacrifice at the suburban altars and ancestral temple, invariably claimed illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 建甯令章華上奏諫曰：「拜三妃以臨軒，祀宗廟而稱疾，非祗肅之道。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Jianning, Zhang Hua, submitted a memorial of remonstrance saying: "You bow to the three consorts when facing the throne, yet claim illness when sacrificing at the ancestral temple—this is not the way of reverence and dignity.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate of Jianning, Zhang Hua, submitted a memorial of remonstrance saying: "You bow to the three consorts when facing the throne, yet claim illness when sacrificing at the ancestral temple—this is not the way of reverence and dignity.

sentences.zh: 」後主怒而斬之。

translations.literal: " Houzhu was enraged and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: " Houzhu was enraged and executed him.

sentences.zh: 又引江總、孔範等內宴，無複尊卑之序，號為狎客，專以詩酒為娛，不恤國政。

translations.literal: He also invited Jiang Zong, Kong Fan, and others to inner banquets without any order of senior and junior, calling them intimate guests; he devoted himself solely to poetry and wine for amusement, heedless of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He also invited Jiang Zong, Kong Fan, and others to inner banquets without any order of senior and junior, calling them intimate guests; he devoted himself solely to poetry and wine for amusement, heedless of state affairs.

sentences.zh: 秘書監傅縡上書諫曰：「人君者，恭事上帝，子愛下人，省嗜欲，遠邪佞，未明求衣，日旰忘食，是以澤被區宇，慶流子孫。

translations.literal: Director of the Secretariat Fu Zai submitted a memorial of remonstrance saying: "The ruler of men reverently serves the Supreme Lord, loves and cares for subordinates, restrains appetites, keeps far from the wicked and sycophantic, seeks understanding before dawn, and forgets to eat until the sun sets—thereby his grace covers the realm and blessings flow to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Secretariat Fu Zai submitted a memorial of remonstrance saying: "The ruler of men reverently serves the Supreme Lord, loves and cares for subordinates, restrains appetites, keeps far from the wicked and sycophantic, seeks understanding before dawn, and forgets to eat until the sun sets—thereby his grace covers the realm and blessings flow to posterity.

sentences.zh: 陛下頃來，酒色過度，不虔郊廟大神，專媚淫昏之鬼。

translations.literal: Your Majesty of late has indulged excessively in wine and women, is not reverent toward the great spirits of the suburban altars and ancestral temple, but devotes yourself solely to licentious and deluded ghosts.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty of late has indulged excessively in wine and women, is not reverent toward the great spirits of the suburban altars and ancestral temple, but devotes yourself solely to licentious and deluded ghosts.

sentences.zh: 小人在側，宦豎擅權，惡誠直如仇讎，視時人如草芥。

translations.literal: Petty men are at your side; eunuchs usurp authority; you hate the sincere and upright as enemies and regard people of the age as mere weeds.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men are at your side; eunuchs usurp authority; you hate the sincere and upright as enemies and regard people of the age as mere weeds.

sentences.zh: 後宮曳羅綺，廄馬餘菽粟，百姓流離，轉屍蔽野。

translations.literal: The rear palace trails in silk and brocade; the stables' horses have grain to spare; the common people wander in exile, and corpses of the dead lie scattered across the fields.
translations.idiomatic: The rear palace trails in silk and brocade; the stables' horses have grain to spare; the common people wander in exile, and corpses of the dead lie scattered across the fields.

sentences.zh: 神怒人怨，眾叛親離。

translations.literal: The spirits are angered and people resentful; all abandon you and kin turn away.
translations.idiomatic: The spirits are angered and people resentful; all abandon you and kin turn away.

sentences.zh: 臣恐東南王氣，自斯而盡。

translations.literal: Your servant fears the royal qi of the southeast will from this be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant fears the royal qi of the southeast will from this be exhausted.

sentences.zh: 」後主不聽，驕恣日甚。

translations.literal: " Houzhu would not listen, and his arrogance and willfulness grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: " Houzhu would not listen, and his arrogance and willfulness grew daily.

sentences.zh: 未幾而國滅。

translations.literal: Before long the state was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the state was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 陳司空侯安都，自以有安社稷之功，驕矜日甚，每侍宴酒酣，輒箕踞而坐。

translations.literal: Minister of Works Hou Andu of Chen, considering himself to have the merit of stabilizing the altars of soil and grain, grew daily more arrogant; whenever he attended banquets and became drunk, he would sit with legs spread in the manner of the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Works Hou Andu of Chen, considering himself to have the merit of stabilizing the altars of soil and grain, grew daily more arrogant; whenever he attended banquets and became drunk, he would sit with legs spread in the manner of the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂文帝曰：「何如作臨川王時？

translations.literal: He once said to Emperor Wen: "How does it compare with when you were Prince of Linchuan?
translations.idiomatic: He once said to Emperor Wen: "How does it compare with when you were Prince of Linchuan?

sentences.zh: 」又借華林園水殿，與妻妾賓客置酒於其上，帝甚惡之。

translations.literal: " He also borrowed the water pavilion of the Hualin Garden and held a banquet there with his wives, concubines, and guests—the emperor greatly detested this.
translations.idiomatic: " He also borrowed the water pavilion of the Hualin Garden and held a banquet there with his wives, concubines, and guests—the emperor greatly detested this.

sentences.zh: 後竟誅死。

translations.literal: In the end he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was executed.

sentences.zh: 東魏，後齊文襄帝時為世子，屬神武帝崩，秘不發喪，朝魏帝於鄴。

translations.literal: In Eastern Wei, when Later Qi's Wenxiang Di was heir apparent, as Shenwu Di had died, the death was kept secret and he attended court with the Wei emperor at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In Eastern Wei, when Later Qi's Wenxiang Di was heir apparent, as Shenwu Di had died, the death was kept secret and he attended court with the Wei emperor at Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏帝宴之，文襄起儛。

translations.literal: The Wei emperor feasted him; Wenxiang rose and danced.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei emperor feasted him; Wenxiang rose and danced.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，又朝魏帝於鄴，侍宴而惰。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, he again attended court with the Wei emperor at Ye and was idle and negligent while attending the feast.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne, he again attended court with the Wei emperor at Ye and was idle and negligent while attending the feast.

sentences.zh: 有識者知文襄之不免。

translations.literal: Those with insight knew Wenxiang would not escape destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Those with insight knew Wenxiang would not escape destruction.

sentences.zh: 後果為盜所害。

translations.literal: In the end he was killed by bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he was killed by bandits.

sentences.zh: 神武時，司徒高昂嘗詣相府，將直入門，門者止之。

translations.literal: During Shenwu's time, Minister of Works Gao Ang once went to the chancellor's residence and was about to enter the gate directly when the gatekeeper stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: During Shenwu's time, Minister of Works Gao Ang once went to the chancellor's residence and was about to enter the gate directly when the gatekeeper stopped him.

sentences.zh: 昂怒，引弓射門者，神武不之罪。

translations.literal: Ang was enraged, drew his bow, and shot the gatekeeper; Shenwu did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Ang was enraged, drew his bow, and shot the gatekeeper; Shenwu did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 尋為西魏所殺。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he was killed by Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was killed by Western Wei.

sentences.zh: 後齊後主為周師所迫，至鄴集兵。

translations.literal: Under Later Qi Houzhu, pressed by Zhou troops, he went to Ye to gather troops.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi Houzhu, pressed by Zhou troops, he went to Ye to gather troops.

sentences.zh: 斛律孝卿勸後主親勞將士，宜流涕慷慨，以感激之，人當自奮。

translations.literal: Hulü Xiaoxiao urged Houzhu to personally encourage the officers and soldiers—he should weep and speak with passion to stir them; people would then rouse themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Hulü Xiaoxiao urged Houzhu to personally encourage the officers and soldiers—he should weep and speak with passion to stir them; people would then rouse themselves.

sentences.zh: 孝卿授之以辭，後主然之。

translations.literal: Xiaoxiao supplied him with words; Houzhu agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoxiao supplied him with words; Houzhu agreed.

sentences.zh: 及對眾，默無所言，因赧然大笑，左右皆哂。

translations.literal: But when facing the assembly, he said nothing and instead blushed and burst into loud laughter; those around him all sneered.
translations.idiomatic: But when facing the assembly, he said nothing and instead blushed and burst into loud laughter; those around him all sneered.

sentences.zh: 將士怒曰：「身尚如此，吾輩何急！

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers said angrily: "Even he is like this—why should we hurry!
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers said angrily: "Even he is like this—why should we hurry!

sentences.zh: 」由是皆無戰心，俄為周師所虜。

translations.literal: " From this all lost the will to fight; soon they were captured by Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: " From this all lost the will to fight; soon they were captured by Zhou troops.

sentences.zh: 煬帝自負才學，每驕天下之士。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang, confident in his own talent and learning, always looked down upon the talented men of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang, confident in his own talent and learning, always looked down upon the talented men of the realm.

sentences.zh: 嘗謂侍臣曰：「天下當謂朕承藉餘緒而有四海耶？

translations.literal: He once said to attending ministers: "Do people under Heaven think I inherited my predecessors' legacy and thereby gained the realm?
translations.idiomatic: He once said to attending ministers: "Do people under Heaven think I inherited my predecessors' legacy and thereby gained the realm?

sentences.zh: 設令朕與士大夫高選，亦當為天子矣。

translations.literal: Suppose I competed in high selection with scholar-officials—I would still become Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose I competed in high selection with scholar-officials—I would still become Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」謂當世之賢，皆所不逮。

translations.literal: " He considered the worthy men of the age all beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: " He considered the worthy men of the age all beneath him.

sentences.zh: 《書》雲：「謂人莫己若者亡。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "He who says no one equals himself will perish.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "He who says no one equals himself will perish.

sentences.zh: 」帝自矜己以輕天下，能不亡乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor, flattering himself and looking down on the realm—could he avoid destruction?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, flattering himself and looking down on the realm—could he avoid destruction?

sentences.zh: 帝又言習吳音，其後竟終於江都，此亦魯襄公終於楚宮之類也。

translations.literal: He also spoke in Wu dialect; afterward he indeed ended at Jiangdu—this too was like Duke Xiang of Lu dying in the Chu palace.
translations.idiomatic: He also spoke in Wu dialect; afterward he indeed met his end at Jiangdu—this too was like Duke Xiang of Lu dying in the Chu palace.

sentences.zh: ○常雨水

translations.literal: ○ Constant rain
translations.idiomatic: ○ Constant rain

sentences.zh: 梁七月，雨，至十月乃霽。

translations.literal: In Liang, in the seventh month, it rained until the tenth month before clearing.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang, in the seventh month, it rained until the tenth month before clearing.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「陰氣強積，然後生水雨之災。

translations.literal: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "When yin qi accumulates in strength, then the calamity of water and rain follows.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "When yin qi accumulates in strength, then the calamity of water and rain follows.

sentences.zh: 」時武帝頻年興師，是歲又大舉北伐，諸軍頗捷，而士卒罷敝，百姓怨望，陰氣畜積之應也。

translations.literal: " At that time Emperor Wu repeatedly mobilized troops; that year he also launched a great northern expedition. Though the armies achieved some victories, soldiers and officers were exhausted and the common people were filled with resentment—this was the response to yin qi accumulating.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Emperor Wu repeatedly mobilized troops; that year he also launched a great northern expedition. Though the armies achieved some victories, soldiers and officers were exhausted and the common people were filled with resentment—this was the omen corresponding to yin qi accumulating.

sentences.zh: 陳八月，大雨霪霖。

translations.literal: In Chen, in the eighth month, heavy rains fell in torrents.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen, in the eighth month, heavy rains fell in torrents.

sentences.zh: 時始興王叔陵驕恣，陰氣盛強之應也。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Shixing Wang Shuling was arrogant and willful—this was the response to yin qi growing powerful.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Shixing Wang Shuling was arrogant and willful—this was the omen corresponding to yin qi growing powerful.

sentences.zh: 明年，宣帝崩，後主立。

translations.literal: The next year, Emperor Xuan died and Houzhu ascended.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, Emperor Xuan died and Houzhu ascended.

sentences.zh: 叔陵刺後主於喪次。

translations.literal: Shuling stabbed Houzhu at the mourning hall.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling stabbed Houzhu at the mourning hall.

sentences.zh: 宮人救之，亻堇而獲免。

translations.literal: Palace women rescued him and he barely escaped with his life.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women rescued him and he barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 叔陵出閤，就東府作亂。

translations.literal: Shuling left the pavilion and raised rebellion at the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Shuling left the pavilion and raised rebellion at the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 後主令蕭摩訶破之，死者千數。

translations.literal: Houzhu ordered Xiao Mohe to defeat him; those killed numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu ordered Xiao Mohe to defeat him; those killed numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 東魏秋，大雨七十餘日，元瑾、劉思逸謀殺後齊文襄之應也。

translations.literal: In Eastern Wei, in autumn, heavy rain fell for more than seventy days—this was the response to Yuan Jin and Liu Siyi's plot to kill Later Qi's Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Eastern Wei, in autumn, heavy rain fell for more than seventy days—this was the omen corresponding to Yuan Jin and Liu Siyi's plot to kill Later Qi's Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 後齊六月庚子，大雨，晝夜不息，至甲辰。

translations.literal: Under Later Qi, on the gengzi day of the sixth month, heavy rain fell day and night without ceasing until the jiachen day.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi, on the gengzi day of the sixth month, heavy rain fell day and night without ceasing until the jiachen day.

sentences.zh: 山東大水，人多餓死。

translations.literal: Shandong suffered great floods and many people died of starvation.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong suffered great floods and many people died of starvation.

sentences.zh: 是歲，突厥寇并州，陰戎作梗，此其應也。

translations.literal: That year, the Turks raided Bing Province and the northern barbarians caused trouble—this was the response.
translations.idiomatic: That year, the Turks raided Bing Province and the northern barbarians caused trouble—this was the corresponding omen.

sentences.zh: 天統三年十月，積陰大雨。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Tiantong, accumulated yin brought heavy rain.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the third year of Tiantong, accumulated yin brought heavy rain.

sentences.zh: 胡太后淫亂之所感也。

translations.literal: This was caused by Empress Dowager Hu's licentious disorder.
translations.idiomatic: This was caused by Empress Dowager Hu's licentious disorder.

sentences.zh: 七月，大霖雨，水澇，人戶流亡。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, great torrential rains caused flooding; households fled in exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, great torrential rains caused flooding; households fled in exile.

sentences.zh: 是時駱提婆、韓長鸞等用事，小人專政之罰也。

translations.literal: At that time Luo Tiba, Han Changluan, and others held power—this was the punishment for petty men monopolizing government.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Luo Tiba, Han Changluan, and others held power—this was the punishment for petty men monopolizing government.

sentences.zh: 後周七月，霖雨三旬。

translations.literal: Under Later Zhou, in the seventh month, torrential rain fell for thirty days.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Zhou, in the seventh month, torrential rain fell for thirty days.

sentences.zh: 時衛刺王直潛謀逆亂。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Wei of Weichi Zhi secretly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Wei of Weichi Zhi secretly plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 屬帝幸雲陽宮，以其徒襲肅章門，尉遲運逆拒破之。

translations.literal: As the emperor was at the Yunyang Palace, Zhi's followers attacked the Suzhang Gate; Yuchi Yun resisted and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: As the emperor was at the Yunyang Palace, Zhi's followers attacked the Suzhang Gate; Yuchi Yun resisted and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 其日雨霽。

translations.literal: That day the rain cleared.
translations.idiomatic: That day the rain cleared.

sentences.zh: ○大雨雪

translations.literal: ○ Heavy snow
translations.idiomatic: ○ Heavy snow

sentences.zh: 梁三月，大雪，平地三尺。

translations.literal: In Liang, in the third month, heavy snow fell three feet deep on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang, in the third month, heavy snow fell three feet deep on level ground.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「庶征之常，雨也，然尤甚焉。

translations.literal: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Among the ordinary portents, rain is common—but this is especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Among the ordinary portents, rain is common—but this is especially severe.

sentences.zh: 雨，陰也；

translations.literal: Rain is yin;
translations.idiomatic: Rain is yin;

sentences.zh: 雪，又陰畜積甚盛也。

translations.literal: snow is yin accumulated to an even greater extreme.
translations.idiomatic: snow is yin accumulated to an even greater extreme.

sentences.zh: 皆妾不妾、臣不臣之應。

translations.literal: Both are responses to consorts not acting as consorts and ministers not acting as ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Both are omens corresponding to consorts not acting as consorts and ministers not acting as ministers.

sentences.zh: 」時義州刺史文僧朗以州叛于魏，臣不臣之應也。

translations.literal: " At that time the Inspector of Yi Province Wen Senglang rebelled with his province to Wei—this was the response to ministers not acting as ministers.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the Inspector of Yi Province Wen Senglang rebelled with his province to Wei—this was the omen corresponding to ministers not acting as ministers.

sentences.zh: 七月，青州雪，害苗稼。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, snow fell in Qing Province, damaging crops.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, snow fell in Qing Province, damaging crops.

sentences.zh: 是時交州刺史李賁舉兵反，僭尊號，置百官，擊之不能克。

translations.literal: At that time the Inspector of Jiao Province Li Ben raised troops in rebellion, presumptuously assumed an imperial title, and established a full bureaucracy; attacks against him could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Inspector of Jiao Province Li Ben raised troops in rebellion, presumptuously assumed an imperial title, and established a full bureaucracy; attacks against him could not succeed.

sentences.zh: 十年十二月，大雪，平地三尺。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the tenth year, heavy snow fell three feet deep on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the tenth year, heavy snow fell three feet deep on level ground.

sentences.zh: 是時邵陵王綸、湘東王繹、武陵王紀並權侔人主，頗為驕恣，皇太子甚惡之，帝不能抑損。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Shaoling Wang Lun, Prince Xiangdong Wang Yi, and Prince Wuling Wang Ji all wielded authority equal to the ruler and were quite arrogant and willful; the crown prince greatly detested them, but the emperor could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Shaoling Wang Lun, Prince Xiangdong Wang Yi, and Prince Wuling Wang Ji all wielded authority equal to the ruler and were quite arrogant and willful; the crown prince greatly detested them, but the emperor could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 上天見變，帝又不悟。

translations.literal: Heaven displayed transformations, yet the emperor did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven displayed transformations, yet the emperor did not heed them.

sentences.zh: 及侯景之亂，諸王各擁強兵，外有赴援之名，內無勤王之實，委棄君父，自相屠滅，國竟以亡。

translations.literal: When the rebellion of Hou Jing arose, the princes each held strong armies—outwardly in the name of rescue, inwardly without any real intent to serve the ruler; they abandoned their sovereign and father and slaughtered one another, and the state was ultimately destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebellion of Hou Jing arose, the princes each held strong armies—outwardly in the name of rescue, inwardly without any real intent to serve the ruler; they abandoned their sovereign and father and slaughtered one another, and the state was ultimately destroyed.

sentences.zh: 東魏五月，大雪。

translations.literal: In Eastern Wei, in the fifth month, heavy snow fell.
translations.idiomatic: In Eastern Wei, in the fifth month, heavy snow fell.

sentences.zh: 時後齊神武作宰，發卒十余萬築鄴城，百姓怨思之徵也。

translations.literal: At that time Later Qi's Shenwu served as chief minister and conscripted more than a hundred thousand corvée laborers to build Ye City—this was a sign of the common people's resentment and sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Later Qi's Shenwu served as chief minister and conscripted more than a hundred thousand corvée laborers to build Ye City—this was a sign of the common people's resentment and sorrow.

sentences.zh: 二月，大雪，人畜凍死，道路相望。

translations.literal: In the second month, heavy snow fell; people and livestock froze to death, and corpses lined the roads.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, heavy snow fell; people and livestock froze to death, and corpses lined the roads.

sentences.zh: 時後齊霸政，而步落稽舉兵反，寇亂數州，人多死亡。

translations.literal: At that time Later Qi held hegemonic power, and Buluoji raised troops in rebellion, raiding and troubling several provinces; many people died.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Later Qi held hegemonic power, and Buluoji raised troops in rebellion, raiding and troubling several provinces; many people died.

sentences.zh: 後齊河清二年二月，大雪連雨，南北千餘裡，平地數尺，繁霜晝下。

translations.literal: Under Later Qi, in the second month of the second year of Heqing, heavy snow and continuous rain extended more than a thousand li north and south; level ground was covered several feet deep, and heavy frost fell even by day.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi, in the second month of the second year of Heqing, heavy snow and continuous rain extended more than a thousand li north and south; level ground was covered several feet deep, and heavy frost fell even by day.

sentences.zh: 是時突厥木杆可汗與周師入并州，殺掠吏人，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: At that time the Turkic Khan Mukan entered Bingzhou with Zhou troops, killing and plundering officials and people beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Turkic Khan Mukan entered Bingzhou with Zhou troops, killing and plundering officials and people beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 天統二年十一月，大雪；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the second year of Tiantong, heavy snow fell;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of the second year of Tiantong, heavy snow fell;

sentences.zh: 三年正月，又大雪，平地二尺；

translations.literal: in the first month of the third year, heavy snow fell again, two feet deep on level ground;
translations.idiomatic: in the first month of the third year, heavy snow fell again, two feet deep on level ground;

sentences.zh: 正月，又大雪。

translations.literal: in the first month, heavy snow fell again.
translations.idiomatic: in the first month, heavy snow fell again.

sentences.zh: 是時馮淑妃、陸令萱內制朝政，陰氣盛積，故天變屢見，雷雨不時。

translations.literal: At that time Consort Feng and Lu Lingxuan controlled court affairs from within; yin qi accumulated in strength—therefore heavenly transformations appeared repeatedly and thunder and rain came at improper times.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Consort Feng and Lu Lingxuan controlled court affairs from within; yin qi accumulated in strength—therefore heavenly transformations appeared repeatedly and thunder and rain came at improper times.

sentences.zh: 陳七月，大雨；

translations.literal: In Chen, in the seventh month, heavy rain fell;
translations.idiomatic: In Chen, in the seventh month, heavy rain fell;

sentences.zh: 震萬安陵華表，又震慧日寺刹，瓦官寺重閤門下一女子震死。

translations.literal: lightning struck the ornamental column at the Wanan Mausoleum and the stupa at the Huiri Temple; a woman below the double gate of the Waguang Temple was killed by lightning.
translations.idiomatic: lightning struck the ornamental column at the Wanan Mausoleum and the stupa at the Huiri Temple; a woman below the double gate of the Waguang Temple was killed by lightning.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「雷雨霹靂丘陵者，逆先人令，為火殺人者，人君用讒言殺正人。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When thunder, rain, and lightning strike hills and mounds—when fire kills people in violation of ancestral commands—the ruler uses slanderous words to kill upright men.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When thunder, rain, and lightning strike hills and mounds—when fire kills people in violation of ancestral commands—the ruler uses slanderous words to kill upright men.

sentences.zh: 」時蔡景曆以奸邪任用，右僕射陸繕以讒毀獲譴，發病而死。

translations.literal: " At that time Cai Jingli was employed through wickedness; Right Vice Director Lu Chuo was condemned through slander, fell ill, and died.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Cai Jingli was employed through wickedness; Right Vice Director Lu Chuo was condemned through slander, fell ill, and died.

sentences.zh: 十年三月，震武庫。

translations.literal: In the third month of the tenth year, lightning struck the armory.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the tenth year, lightning struck the armory.

sentences.zh: 時帝好兵，頻年北伐，內外虛竭，將士勞敝。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor loved warfare and repeatedly launched northern expeditions; within and without were emptied and depleted, and soldiers and officers were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor loved warfare and repeatedly launched northern expeditions; within and without were emptied and depleted, and soldiers and officers were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 既克淮南，又進圖彭、汴，毛喜切諫，不納。

translations.literal: After capturing Huainan, he further advanced to besiege Peng and Bian; Mao Xi remonstrated urgently but was not heeded.
