translations.idiomatic: After capturing Huainan, he further advanced to besiege Peng and Bian; Mao Xi remonstrated urgently but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 由是吳明徹諸軍皆沒，遂失淮南之地。

translations.literal: Thereupon the armies of Wu Mingche and others were all destroyed, and Huainan was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the armies of Wu Mingche and others were all destroyed, and Huainan was lost.

sentences.zh: 武庫者，兵器之所聚也，而震之，天戒若曰，宜戢兵以安百姓。

translations.literal: The armory is where weapons are gathered—yet lightning struck it. Heaven's warning seemed to say: restrain the armies to pacify the common people.
translations.idiomatic: The armory is where weapons are gathered—yet lightning struck it. Heaven's warning seemed to say: restrain the armies to pacify the common people.

sentences.zh: 帝不悟，又大興軍旅，其年六月，又震太皇寺刹、莊嚴寺露槃、重陽閣東樓、鴻臚府門。

translations.literal: The emperor did not understand and again raised armies on a vast scale; that year in the sixth month, lightning again struck the stupa of the Taihuang Temple, the dew basin of the Zhuangyan Temple, the eastern tower of the Chongyang Pavilion, and the gate of the Honglu Office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed the warning and again raised armies on a vast scale; that year in the sixth month, lightning again struck the stupa of the Taihuang Temple, the dew basin of the Zhuangyan Temple, the eastern tower of the Chongyang Pavilion, and the gate of the Honglu Office.

sentences.zh: 太皇、莊嚴二寺，陳國奉佛之所，重陽閣每所遊宴，鴻臚賓客禮儀之所在，而同歲震者，天戒若曰，國威已喪，不務修德，後必有恃佛道，耽宴樂，棄禮儀而亡國者。

translations.literal: The Taihuang and Zhuangyan temples were where Chen worshipped Buddhism; the Chongyang Pavilion was where the ruler often held banquets; the Honglu Office was where guest ritual was conducted—yet all were struck in the same year. Heaven's warning seemed to say: the state's prestige is already lost; if you do not cultivate virtue, afterward there will be one who relies on Buddhism, indulges in banquets and pleasure, abandons ritual propriety, and loses the state.
translations.idiomatic: The Taihuang and Zhuangyan temples were where Chen worshipped Buddhism; the Chongyang Pavilion was where the ruler often held banquets; the Honglu Office was where guest ritual was conducted—yet all were struck in the same year. Heaven's warning seemed to say: the state's prestige is already lost; if you do not cultivate virtue, afterward there will be one who relies on Buddhism, indulges in banquets and pleasure, abandons ritual propriety, and loses the state.

sentences.zh: 陳之君臣竟不悟。

translations.literal: Chen's rulers and ministers ultimately did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: Chen's rulers and ministers ultimately did not heed the warnings.

sentences.zh: 至後主之代，災異屢起，懼而於太皇寺捨身為奴，以祈冥助，不恤國政，耽酒色，棄禮法，不修鄰好，以取敗亡。

translations.literal: In Houzhu's time, calamities and anomalies arose repeatedly; in fear he offered himself as a slave at the Taihuang Temple to seek aid from the unseen, heedless of state affairs, indulging in wine and women, abandoning ritual law, and neglecting good relations with neighbors—thereby bringing defeat and destruction.
translations.idiomatic: In Houzhu's time, calamities and anomalies arose repeatedly; in fear he offered himself as a slave at the Taihuang Temple to seek aid from the unseen, heedless of state affairs, indulging in wine and women, abandoning ritual law, and neglecting good relations with neighbors—thereby bringing defeat and destruction.

sentences.zh: 齊夏，震丞相段孝先南門柱。

translations.literal: In Qi, in summer, lightning struck the southern gate pillar of Chancellor Duan Xiaoxian.
translations.idiomatic: In Qi, in summer, lightning struck the southern gate pillar of Chancellor Duan Xiaoxian.

sentences.zh: 京房《易傳》曰：「震擊貴臣門及屋者，不出三年，佞臣被誅。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When lightning strikes the gate and house of an exalted minister, within three years the sycophantic minister will be executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Commentary on the Changes says: "When lightning strikes the gate and house of an exalted minister, within three years the sycophantic minister will be executed.

sentences.zh: 」後歲，和士開被戮。

translations.literal: " The following year, He Shikai was executed.
translations.idiomatic: " The following year, He Shikai was executed.

sentences.zh: ○木冰

translations.literal: ○ Tree ice
translations.idiomatic: ○ Tree ice

sentences.zh: 東魏冬，天雨木冰。

translations.literal: In Eastern Wei, in winter, tree ice fell from the sky.
translations.idiomatic: In Eastern Wei, in winter, tree ice fell from the sky.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「陰之盛而凝滯也。

translations.literal: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "This is yin at its strongest, congealing and stagnating.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "This is yin at its strongest, congealing and stagnating.

sentences.zh: 木者少陽，貴臣象也。

translations.literal: Wood is lesser yang—the symbol of exalted ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Wood is lesser yang—the symbol of exalted ministers.

sentences.zh: 將有害，則陰氣脅木，木先寒，故得雨而冰襲之。

translations.literal: When harm is about to come, yin qi presses upon wood; wood grows cold first, and therefore receives rain with ice coating it.
translations.idiomatic: When harm is about to come, yin qi presses upon wood; wood grows cold first, and therefore receives rain with ice coating it.

sentences.zh: 木冰一名介，介者兵之象也。

translations.literal: Tree ice is also called jie—jie is the symbol of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: Tree ice is also called jie—jie is the symbol of warfare.

sentences.zh: 」時司徒侯景制河南，及神武不豫，文襄懼其為亂而征之，景因舉兵反。

translations.literal: " At that time Minister of Works Hou Jing controlled Henan; when Shenwu fell ill, Wenxiang feared he would cause trouble and summoned him; Jing therefore raised troops in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Minister of Works Hou Jing controlled Henan; when Shenwu fell ill, Wenxiang feared he would cause trouble and summoned him; Jing therefore raised troops in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 豫州刺史高元成、襄州刺史李密、廣州刺史暴顯並為景所執辱，貴臣有害之應也。

translations.literal: The Inspector of Yu Province Gao Yuancheng, the Inspector of Xiang Province Li Mi, and the Inspector of Guang Province Bao Xian were all seized and humiliated by Jing—this was the response to harm coming to exalted ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector of Yu Province Gao Yuancheng, the Inspector of Xiang Province Li Mi, and the Inspector of Guang Province Bao Xian were all seized and humiliated by Jing—this was the omen corresponding to harm coming to exalted ministers.

sentences.zh: 其後左僕射慕容紹宗與景戰于渦陽，俘斬五萬。

translations.literal: Afterward Left Vice Director Murong Shaozong fought Jing at Woyang and captured and beheaded fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Left Vice Director Murong Shaozong fought Jing at Woyang and captured and beheaded fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 後齊，雨木冰三日。

translations.literal: Under Later Qi, tree ice fell for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi, tree ice fell for three days.

sentences.zh: 初，清河王岳為高歸彥所譖，是歲以憂死。

translations.literal: Earlier, Prince Qinghe Wang Yue had been slandered by Gao Guiyan; that year he died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Prince Qinghe Wang Yue had been slandered by Gao Guiyan; that year he died of grief.

sentences.zh: 武平元年冬，雨木冰；

translations.literal: In the winter of the first year of Wuping, tree ice fell;
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the first year of Wuping, tree ice fell;

sentences.zh: 明年二月，又木冰。

translations.literal: in the second month of the next year, tree ice fell again.
translations.idiomatic: in the second month of the next year, tree ice fell again.

sentences.zh: 時錄尚書事和士開專政。

translations.literal: At that time He Shikai, Recorder of Affairs, monopolized government.
translations.idiomatic: At that time He Shikai, Recorder of Affairs, monopolized government.

sentences.zh: 其年七月，太保、琅邪王儼矯詔殺之。

translations.literal: That year in the seventh month, Grand Tutor Prince Langye Wang Yan used a forged edict to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: That year in the seventh month, Grand Tutor Prince Langye Wang Yan used a forged edict to kill him.

sentences.zh: 領軍大將軍庫狄伏連、尚書右僕射馮子琮並坐儼賜死。

translations.literal: Commander-in-Chief Kudi Fulian and Right Vice Director Feng Zicong were both executed on Yan's account.
translations.idiomatic: Commander-in-Chief Kudi Fulian and Right Vice Director Feng Zicong were both executed on Yan's account.

sentences.zh: 九月，儼亦遇害。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yan also met with violent death.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Yan also met with violent death.

sentences.zh: 六年、七年，頻歲春冬木冰。

translations.literal: In the sixth and seventh years, tree ice fell repeatedly in spring and winter.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth and seventh years, tree ice fell repeatedly in spring and winter.

sentences.zh: 其年周師入晉陽，因平鄴都。

translations.literal: That year Zhou troops entered Jinyang and then pacified the capital at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhou troops entered Jinyang and then pacified the capital at Ye.

sentences.zh: 後主走青州，貴臣死散，州郡被兵者不可勝數。

translations.literal: Houzhu fled to Qing Province; exalted ministers died and scattered; commanderies and prefectures struck by warfare were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu fled to Qing Province; exalted ministers died and scattered; commanderies and prefectures struck by warfare were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: ○大雨雹

translations.literal: ○ Heavy hail
translations.idiomatic: ○ Heavy hail

sentences.zh: 梁四月，大雨雹。

translations.literal: In Liang, in the fourth month, heavy hail fell.
translations.idiomatic: In Liang, in the fourth month, heavy hail fell.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「雹，陰脅陽之象也。

translations.literal: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Hail is the symbol of yin pressing upon yang.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "Hail is the symbol of yin pressing upon yang.

sentences.zh: 」時帝數捨身為奴，拘信佛法，為沙門所制。

translations.literal: " At that time the emperor repeatedly offered himself as a slave, clung to Buddhist faith, and was controlled by monks.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the emperor repeatedly offered himself as a slave, clung to Buddhist faith, and was controlled by monks.

sentences.zh: 陳六月，大雨雹；

translations.literal: In Chen, in the sixth month, heavy hail fell;
translations.idiomatic: In Chen, in the sixth month, heavy hail fell;

sentences.zh: 十年四月，又大雨雹；

translations.literal: in the fourth month of the tenth year, heavy hail fell again;
translations.idiomatic: in the fourth month of the tenth year, heavy hail fell again;

sentences.zh: 十三年九月，又雨雹。

translations.literal: in the ninth month of the thirteenth year, hail fell again.
translations.idiomatic: in the ninth month of the thirteenth year, hail fell again.

sentences.zh: 時始興王叔陵驕恣，陰結死士，圖為不逞，帝又寵遇之，故天三見變。

translations.literal: At that time Prince Shixing Wang Shuling was arrogant and willful, secretly gathered death-pledged warriors, and plotted mischief; the emperor also favored and indulged him—therefore Heaven displayed transformations three times.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Shixing Wang Shuling was arrogant and willful, secretly gathered death-pledged warriors, and plotted mischief; the emperor also favored and indulged him—therefore Heaven displayed transformations three times.

sentences.zh: 帝不悟。

translations.literal: The emperor did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed the warnings.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，叔陵果為亂逆。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Shuling indeed raised rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, Shuling indeed raised rebellion.

sentences.zh: ○服妖

translations.literal: ○ Clothing anomalies
translations.idiomatic: ○ Clothing anomalies

sentences.zh: 後齊婁後臥疾，寢衣無故自舉。

translations.literal: Under Later Qi, when Empress Lou lay ill, her sleeping garment rose without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi, when Empress Lou lay ill, her sleeping garment rose without cause.

sentences.zh: 俄而後崩。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the empress died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the empress died.

sentences.zh: 文宣帝末年，衣錦綺，傅粉黛，數為胡服，微行市裡。

translations.literal: In the final years of Wenxuan Di, he wore brocade and silk, applied powder and rouge, often dressed in barbarian clothing, and walked incognito through the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: In the final years of Wenxuan Di, he wore brocade and silk, applied powder and rouge, often dressed in barbarian clothing, and walked incognito through the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 粉黛者，婦人之飾，陽為陰事，君變為臣之象也。

translations.literal: Powder and rouge are women's adornments—yang doing yin's affairs is the symbol of the ruler transforming into a minister.
translations.idiomatic: Powder and rouge are women's adornments—yang doing yin's affairs is the symbol of the ruler transforming into a minister.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，太子嗣位，被廢為濟南王。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, the crown prince succeeded; he was deposed and made Prince of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died, the crown prince succeeded; he was deposed and made Prince of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 又齊氏出自陰山，胡服者，將反初服也。

translations.literal: Also, Qi originated from Yinshan; barbarian dress meant a return to original garb.
translations.idiomatic: Also, Qi originated from Yinshan; barbarian dress meant a return to original garb.

sentences.zh: 錦彩非帝王之法服，微服者布衣之事，齊亡之效也。

translations.literal: Brocade and colored silk are not the proper robes of emperors and kings; incognito dress is the affair of commoners—this was the effect of Qi's destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade and colored silk are not the proper robes of emperors and kings; incognito dress is the affair of commoners—this was the effect of Qi's destruction.

sentences.zh: 後主好令宮人以白越布折額，狀如髽幗；

translations.literal: Houzhu liked to have palace women fold white ramie cloth across their foreheads in the shape of a mourning coiffure;
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu liked to have palace women fold white ramie cloth across their foreheads in the shape of a mourning coiffure;

sentences.zh: 又為白蓋。

translations.literal: he also had them make white canopies.
translations.idiomatic: he also had them make white canopies.

sentences.zh: 此二者，喪禍之服也。

translations.literal: Both of these are garments of mourning and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Both of these are garments of mourning and calamity.

sentences.zh: 後主果為周武帝所滅，父子同時被害。

translations.literal: Houzhu was indeed destroyed by Emperor Wu of Zhou; father and son were killed at the same time.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu was indeed destroyed by Emperor Wu of Zhou; father and son were killed at the same time.

sentences.zh: 武平時，後主于苑內作貧兒村，親衣襤褸之服而行乞其間，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: During the Wuping era, Houzhu built a Poor Man's Village in the garden, personally wearing tattered clothes and going begging there for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wuping era, Houzhu built a Poor Man's Village in the garden, personally wearing tattered clothes and going begging there for amusement.

sentences.zh: 多令人服烏衣，以相執縛。

translations.literal: He also had many people wear black clothing and bind one another as captives.
translations.idiomatic: He also had many people wear black clothing and bind one another as captives.

sentences.zh: 後主果為周所敗，被虜于長安而死；

translations.literal: Houzhu was indeed defeated by Zhou, captured at Chang'an, and died there;
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu was indeed defeated by Zhou, captured at Chang'an, and died there;

sentences.zh: 妃後窮困，至以賣燭為業。

translations.literal: consorts and empresses fell into destitution, even selling candles for a living.
translations.idiomatic: consorts and empresses fell into destitution, even selling candles for a living.

sentences.zh: 後周，服冕二十有四旒，車服旗鼓，皆以二十四為節。

translations.literal: Under Later Zhou, the ceremonial cap had twenty-four tassels; chariots, robes, banners, and drums all used twenty-four as their measure.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Zhou, the ceremonial cap had twenty-four tassels; chariots, robes, banners, and drums all used twenty-four as their measure.

sentences.zh: 侍衛之官，服五色，雜以紅紫。

translations.literal: Guard officials wore five colors mixed with red and purple.
translations.idiomatic: Guard officials wore five colors mixed with red and purple.

sentences.zh: 令天下車以大木為輪，不施輻。

translations.literal: He ordered carts throughout the realm to use large logs as wheels without spokes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered carts throughout the realm to use large logs as wheels without spokes.

sentences.zh: 朝士不得佩綬，婦人墨妝黃眉。

translations.literal: Court officials could not wear sashes; women used black makeup and yellow eyebrows.
translations.idiomatic: Court officials could not wear sashes; women used black makeup and yellow eyebrows.

sentences.zh: 又造下帳，如送終之具，令五皇后各居其一，實宗廟祭器於前，帝親讀版而祭之。

translations.literal: He also made lower tents like funeral equipment, had the five empresses each occupy one, placed ancestral temple ritual vessels before them, and the emperor personally read the spirit tablets and sacrificed to them.
translations.idiomatic: He also made lower tents like funeral equipment, had the five empresses each occupy one, placed ancestral temple ritual vessels before them, and the emperor personally read the spirit tablets and sacrificed to them.

sentences.zh: 又將五輅載婦人，身率左右步從。

translations.literal: He also loaded the five imperial chariots with women and personally walked behind with his attendants.
translations.idiomatic: He also loaded the five imperial chariots with women and personally walked behind with his attendants.

sentences.zh: 又倒懸雞及碎瓦于車上，觀其作聲，以為笑樂。

translations.literal: He also hung chickens upside down and broken tiles on carts, watching them make noise for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He also hung chickens upside down and broken tiles on carts, watching them make noise for amusement.

sentences.zh: 皆服妖也。

translations.literal: All of these were clothing anomalies.
translations.idiomatic: All of these were clothing anomalies.

sentences.zh: 帝尋暴崩，而政由於隋，周之法度，皆悉改易。

translations.literal: The emperor soon died suddenly; thereafter government passed to Sui, and all Zhou institutions were completely changed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor soon died suddenly; thereafter government passed to Sui, and all Zhou institutions were completely changed.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，房陵王勇之在東宮，及宜陽公王世積家，婦人所有領巾制同槊幡軍幟。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang, women in the households of Prince Fangling Yong at the Eastern Palace and Duke Yiyang Wang Shiji had head scarves made like spear banners and military flags.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang, women in the households of Prince Fangling Yong at the Eastern Palace and Duke Yiyang Wang Shiji had head scarves made like spear banners and military flags.

sentences.zh: 婦人為陰，臣象也，而服兵幟，臣有兵禍之應矣。

translations.literal: Women represent yin and are the symbol of ministers—yet they wore military banners; this was the response to ministers facing military calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Women represent yin and are the symbol of ministers—yet they wore military banners; this was the omen corresponding to ministers facing military calamity.

sentences.zh: 勇竟而遇害，世積坐伏誅。

translations.literal: Yong was ultimately killed; Shiji was executed for his crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was ultimately killed; Shiji was executed for his crimes.

sentences.zh: ○雞禍

translations.literal: ○ Chicken calamities
translations.idiomatic: ○ Chicken calamities

sentences.zh: 開皇中，有人上書，言頻歲已來，雞鳴不鼓翅，類腋下有物而妨之，翮不得舉，肘腑之臣，當為變矣。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang, someone submitted a memorial saying that in recent years roosters crowed without flapping their wings—as if something under the armpit obstructed them and the wings could not rise—the ministers close to the ruler's side would undergo transformation.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang, someone submitted a memorial saying that in recent years roosters crowed without flapping their wings—as if something under the armpit obstructed them and the wings could not rise—the ministers close to the ruler's side would undergo transformation.

sentences.zh: 書奏不省。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but not examined.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted but not examined.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「雞鳴不鼓翅，國有大害。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When roosters crow without flapping their wings, the state will suffer great harm.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When roosters crow without flapping their wings, the state will suffer great harm.

sentences.zh: 」其後大臣多被夷滅，諸王廢黜，太子幽廢。

translations.literal: " Afterward many great ministers were exterminated, princes were deposed, and the crown prince was secretly deposed.
translations.idiomatic: " Afterward many great ministers were exterminated, princes were deposed, and the crown prince was secretly deposed.

sentences.zh: 大業初，天下雞多夜鳴，京房《易飛候》曰：「雞夜鳴，急令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, roosters throughout the realm crowed at night. Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When roosters crow at night, urgent commands follow.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Daye, roosters throughout the realm crowed at night. Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When roosters crow at night, urgent commands follow.

sentences.zh: 」又雲：「昏而鳴，百姓有事；

translations.literal: " It also says: "When they crow at dusk, the common people have troubles;
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "When they crow at dusk, the common people have troubles;

sentences.zh: 人定鳴，多戰；

translations.literal: when they crow at the hour of human rest, much warfare follows;
translations.idiomatic: when they crow at the hour of human rest, much warfare follows;

sentences.zh: 夜半鳴，流血漫漫。

translations.literal: when they crow at midnight, blood flows endlessly.
translations.idiomatic: when they crow at midnight, blood flows endlessly.

sentences.zh: 」及中年已後，軍國多務，用度不足，於是急令暴賦，責成守宰，百姓不聊生矣，各起而為盜，戰爭不息，屍骸被野。

translations.literal: " From mid-age onward, military and state affairs multiplied and expenses were insufficient; therefore urgent commands and harsh levies were imposed, holding district magistrates accountable—the common people could not survive, each rose as bandits, warfare never ceased, and corpses covered the fields.
translations.idiomatic: " From mid-age onward, military and state affairs multiplied and expenses were insufficient; therefore urgent commands and harsh levies were imposed, holding district magistrates accountable—the common people could not survive, each rose as bandits, warfare never ceased, and corpses covered the fields.

sentences.zh: ○龜孽

translations.literal: ○ Turtle portents
translations.idiomatic: ○ Turtle portents

sentences.zh: 開皇中，掖庭宮每夜有人來挑宮人。

translations.literal: During Kaihuang, at the Rear Palace quarters someone came each night to seduce palace women.
translations.idiomatic: During Kaihuang, at the Rear Palace quarters someone came each night to seduce palace women.

sentences.zh: 宮司以聞。

translations.literal: The palace office reported this.
translations.idiomatic: The palace office reported this.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「門衛甚嚴，人何從而入？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The gate guards are very strict—how could a person enter?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The gate guards are very strict—how could a person enter?

sentences.zh: 當是妖精耳。

translations.literal: It must be a spirit creature.
translations.idiomatic: It must be a spirit creature.

sentences.zh: 」因戒宮人曰：「若逢，但斫之。

translations.literal: " He therefore warned the palace women: "If you encounter it, just hack at it.
translations.idiomatic: " He therefore warned the palace women: "If you encounter it, just hack at it.

sentences.zh: 」其後有物如人，夜來登床，宮人抽刀斫之，若中枯骨。

translations.literal: " Afterward something like a person came at night and climbed onto the bed; a palace woman drew a knife and hacked at it, as if striking dry bone.
translations.idiomatic: " Afterward something like a person came at night and climbed onto the bed; a palace woman drew a knife and hacked at it, as if striking dry bone.

sentences.zh: 其物落床而走，宮人逐之，因入池而沒。

translations.literal: The creature fell from the bed and fled; the palace woman pursued it and it entered a pool and sank.
translations.idiomatic: The creature fell from the bed and fled; the palace woman pursued it and it entered a pool and sank.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝令涸池，得一龜，徑尺餘，其上有刀跡。

translations.literal: The next day the emperor ordered the pool drained and a turtle more than a foot in diameter was found, bearing knife marks on its shell.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the emperor ordered the pool drained and a turtle more than a foot in diameter was found, bearing knife marks on its shell.

sentences.zh: 殺之，遂絕。

translations.literal: It was killed, and the visits ceased.
translations.idiomatic: It was killed, and the visits ceased.

sentences.zh: 龜者水居而靈，陰謀之象，晉王諂媚宮掖求嗣之應雲。

translations.literal: The turtle lives in water and is numinous—the symbol of secret plots; this was the response to Prince Jin's sycophantic advances in the inner palace seeking succession.
translations.idiomatic: The turtle lives in water and is numinous—the symbol of secret plots; this was the omen corresponding to Prince Jin's sycophantic advances in the inner palace seeking succession.

sentences.zh: ○青眚青祥

translations.literal: ○ Green baleful signs and green omens
translations.idiomatic: ○ Green baleful signs and green omens

sentences.zh: 陳四月，群鼠無數，自蔡洲岸入石頭淮，至青塘兩岸。

translations.literal: In Chen, in the fourth month, countless rats from the Cai Isle shore entered Shitou on the Huai River to the banks of Qingtang.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen, in the fourth month, countless rats from the Cai Isle shore entered Shitou on the Huai River to the banks of Qingtang.

sentences.zh: 數日死，隨流出江。

translations.literal: After several days they died and floated out with the current into the river.
translations.idiomatic: After several days they died and floated out with the current into the river.

sentences.zh: 近青祥也。

translations.literal: This approximates a green omen.
translations.idiomatic: This approximates a green omen.

sentences.zh: 京房《易飛候》曰：「鼠無故群居，不穴眾聚者，其君死。

translations.literal: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When rats for no reason gather in groups without burrowing, their ruler will die.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Fang's Flying Omens of the Changes says: "When rats for no reason gather in groups without burrowing, their ruler will die.

sentences.zh: 」未幾而國亡。

translations.literal: " Before long the state perished.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long the state perished.

sentences.zh: ○金沴木

translations.literal: ○ Metal harming wood
translations.idiomatic: ○ Metal harming wood

sentences.zh: 陳秋七月，儀賢堂無故自壓，近金沴木也。

translations.literal: In Chen, in the seventh month of autumn, the Hall of Esteem for the Worthy collapsed without cause—this approximates metal harming wood.
translations.idiomatic: In Chen, in the seventh month of autumn, the Hall of Esteem for the Worthy collapsed without cause—this approximates metal harming wood.

sentences.zh: 時帝盛修宮室，起顯德等五殿，稱為壯麗，百姓失業，故木失其性也。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor lavishly built palaces, erecting five halls including Xiande, calling them magnificent; the common people lost their livelihoods—therefore wood lost its nature.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor lavishly built palaces, erecting five halls including Xiande, calling them magnificent; the common people lost their livelihoods—therefore wood lost its nature.

sentences.zh: 儀賢堂者，禮賢尚齒之謂，無故自壓，天戒若曰，帝好奢侈，不能用賢使能，何用虛名也。

translations.literal: The Hall of Esteem for the Worthy means honoring the worthy and respecting the aged; collapsing without cause—Heaven's warning seemed to say: the emperor loves extravagance and cannot employ the worthy and capable—why keep an empty name?
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Esteem for the Worthy means honoring the worthy and respecting the aged; collapsing without cause—Heaven's warning seemed to say: the emperor loves extravagance and cannot employ the worthy and capable—why keep an empty name?

sentences.zh: 帝不悟，明年竟崩。

translations.literal: The emperor did not understand; the next year he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed the warning; the next year he died.

sentences.zh: 六月，宮內水殿若有刀鋸斫伐之聲，其殿因無故而倒。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, at the water pavilion within the palace there were sounds like knives and saws cutting and chopping; the pavilion then collapsed without cause.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, at the water pavilion within the palace there were sounds like knives and saws cutting and chopping; the pavilion then collapsed without cause.

sentences.zh: 七月，朱雀航又無故自沉。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the Zhuque Bridge also sank without cause.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, the Zhuque Bridge also sank without cause.

sentences.zh: 時後主盛修園囿，不虔宗廟。

translations.literal: At that time Houzhu lavishly built gardens and parks and was not reverent toward the ancestral temple.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Houzhu lavishly built gardens and parks and was not reverent toward the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 水殿者，遊宴之所，朱雀航者，國門之大路，而無故自壞，天戒若曰，宮室毀，津路絕。

translations.literal: The water pavilion is a place for banquets and pleasure; the Zhuque Bridge is the great road of the national gate—yet both were destroyed without cause. Heaven's warning seemed to say: palace buildings destroyed, ferry routes cut off.
translations.idiomatic: The water pavilion is a place for banquets and pleasure; the Zhuque Bridge is the great road of the national gate—yet both were destroyed without cause. Heaven's warning seemed to say: palace buildings destroyed, ferry routes cut off.

sentences.zh: 後主不悟，竟為隋所滅，宮廟為墟。

translations.literal: Houzhu did not understand; in the end he was destroyed by Sui and palaces and temples became ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Houzhu did not heed the warnings; in the end he was destroyed by Sui and palaces and temples became ruins.

sentences.zh: 後齊孝昭帝將誅楊愔，乘車向省，入東門，「Ｗ竿無故自折。

translations.literal: Under Later Qi, when Emperor Xiaozhao was about to execute Yang Yin, riding in his carriage toward the Secretariat, upon entering the Eastern Gate the flagpole broke without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Qi, when Emperor Xiaozhao was about to execute Yang Yin, riding in his carriage toward the Secretariat, upon entering the Eastern Gate the flagpole broke without cause.

sentences.zh: 帝甚惡之，歲餘而崩。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly detested this; little more than a year later he died.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor greatly detested this; little more than a year later he died.

sentences.zh: 河清三年，長廣郡聽事梁忽剝若人狀，太守惡而削去之，明日複然。

translations.literal: In the third year of Heqing, the beam of the administrative hall in Changguang Commandery suddenly peeled away like a human shape; the magistrate detested this and cut it away, but the next day it appeared again.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing, the beam of the administrative hall in Changguang Commandery suddenly peeled away like a human shape; the magistrate detested this and cut it away, but the next day it appeared again.

sentences.zh: 長廣，帝本封也，木為變，不祥之兆。

translations.literal: Changguang was the emperor's original fief; wood transforming was an inauspicious portent.
translations.idiomatic: Changguang was the emperor's original fief; wood transforming was an inauspicious portent.

sentences.zh: 其年帝崩。

translations.literal: That year the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That year the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 秋，穆後將如晉陽，向北宮辭胡太后。

translations.literal: In autumn, Empress Mu was about to go to Jinyang and went to the Northern Palace to bid farewell to Empress Dowager Hu.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, Empress Mu was about to go to Jinyang and went to the Northern Palace to bid farewell to Empress Dowager Hu.

sentences.zh: 至宮內門，所乘七寶車無故陷入于地，牛沒四足。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the inner palace gate, the seven-jeweled carriage she rode sank without cause into the ground; the oxen's four legs were submerged.
translations.idiomatic: Upon reaching the inner palace gate, the seven-jeweled carriage she rode sank without cause into the ground; the oxen's four legs were submerged.

sentences.zh: 是歲齊滅，後被虜于長安。

translations.literal: That year Qi was destroyed; afterward she was captured at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qi was destroyed; afterward she was captured at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 後周，青城門無故自崩。

translations.literal: Under Later Zhou, the Qingcheng Gate collapsed without cause.
translations.idiomatic: Under Later Zhou, the Qingcheng Gate collapsed without cause.

sentences.zh: 青者東方色，春宮之象也。

translations.literal: Green is the color of the East—the symbol of the Spring Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Green is the color of the East—the symbol of the Spring Palace.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子無威儀禮節，青城門無故自崩者，皇太子不勝任之應。

translations.literal: At that time the crown prince lacked dignity, ritual, and propriety; the Qingcheng Gate collapsing without cause was the response to the crown prince being unfit for his role.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the crown prince lacked dignity, ritual, and propriety; the Qingcheng Gate collapsing without cause was the omen corresponding to the crown prince being unfit for his role.

sentences.zh: 帝不悟。

translations.literal: The emperor did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not heed the warning.

sentences.zh: 明年太子嗣位，果為無道。

translations.literal: The next year the crown prince succeeded and indeed behaved without the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the crown prince succeeded and indeed behaved without the Way.

sentences.zh: 周室危亡，實自此始。

translations.literal: The Zhou house's peril and destruction truly began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou house's peril and destruction truly began from this.

sentences.zh: 大業中，齊王暕於東都起第，新構寢堂，其栿無故而折。

translations.literal: During Daye, Prince Qi Yangdi at the Eastern Capital built a residence; in the newly constructed sleeping hall the ridge beam broke without cause.
translations.idiomatic: During Daye, Prince Qi Yangdi at the Eastern Capital built a residence; in the newly constructed sleeping hall the ridge beam broke without cause.

sentences.zh: 時上無太子，天下皆以暕次當立，公卿屬望，暕遂驕恣，呼術者令相，又為厭勝之事。

translations.literal: At that time there was no crown prince; all under Heaven considered Yangdi next in line for installation; public officials looked to him; Yangdi therefore grew arrogant and willful, summoned diviners to read his fate, and also performed sorcery for victory.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was no crown prince; all under Heaven considered Yangdi next in line for installation; public officials looked to him; Yangdi therefore grew arrogant and willful, summoned diviners to read his fate, and also performed sorcery for victory.

sentences.zh: 堂栿無故自折，木失其性，奸謀之應也。

translations.literal: The hall ridge beam breaking without cause—wood losing its nature—was the response to treacherous plotting.
translations.idiomatic: The hall ridge beam breaking without cause—wood losing its nature—was the omen corresponding to treacherous plotting.

sentences.zh: 天見變以戒之，暕不悟，後竟得罪於帝。

translations.literal: Heaven displayed transformations to warn him; Yangdi did not understand; afterward he indeed offended the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven displayed transformations to warn him; Yangdi did not heed them; afterward he indeed offended the emperor.

sentences.zh: 《洪範五行傳》曰：「言之不從，是謂不乂。

translations.literal: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "When words are not followed, this is called lack of governance.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Plan's Transmission on the Five Phases says: "When words are not followed, this is called lack of governance.

sentences.zh: 厥咎僭，厥罰常暘，厥極憂。

translations.literal: The fault is presumption; the punishment is constant drought; the extreme is sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: The fault is presumption; the punishment is constant drought; the extreme is sorrow.

sentences.zh: 時則有詩妖，時則有毛蟲之孽，時則有犬禍。

translations.literal: At such times there are poetic anomalies; at such times there are insect portents; at such times there are dog calamities.
translations.idiomatic: At such times there are poetic anomalies; at such times there are insect portents; at such times there are dog calamities.

sentences.zh: 故有口舌之屙，有白眚白祥。

translations.literal: Therefore there are discharges of the mouth and tongue; there are white baleful signs and white omens.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore there are discharges of the mouth and tongue; there are white baleful signs and white omens.

sentences.zh: 惟木沴金。

translations.literal: Only wood harms metal.
translations.idiomatic: Only wood harms metal.

sentences.zh: ○言不從

translations.literal: ○ Words not followed
translations.idiomatic: ○ Words not followed

sentences.zh: 梁武陵王紀僭即帝位，建元曰天正。

translations.literal: Prince Wuling Wang Ji of Liang presumptuously assumed the imperial title and established the era name Tianzheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Wuling Wang Ji of Liang presumptuously assumed the imperial title and established the era name Tianzheng.

sentences.zh: 永豐侯蕭捴曰：「王不克矣。

translations.literal: Marquis Yongfeng Xiao Zhou said: "Your Highness will not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Marquis Yongfeng Xiao Zhou said: "Your Highness will not succeed.

sentences.zh: 昔桓玄年號大亨，有識者以為'二月了'，而玄之敗，實在仲春。

translations.literal: Formerly Huan Xuan's era name was Daheng; those with insight read it as 'finished in the second month,' and Xuan's defeat indeed came in mid-spring.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Huan Xuan's era name was Daheng; those with insight read it as 'finished in the second month,' and Xuan's defeat indeed came in mid-spring.

sentences.zh: 今日天正，正之為文'一止'，其能久乎！

translations.literal: Today's Tianzheng—as a written character it is 'one stop'—can it last long!
translations.idiomatic: Today's Tianzheng—as a written character it is 'one stop'—can it last long!

sentences.zh: 」果一年而敗。

translations.literal: " Indeed, within a year he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: " Indeed, within a year he was defeated.

sentences.zh: 後齊文宣帝時，太子殷當冠，詔令邢子才為制字。

translations.literal: During Later Qi's Wenxuan Di, when Crown Prince Yin was to receive the capping ceremony, an edict ordered Xing Zicai to compose the style name.
translations.idiomatic: During Later Qi's Wenxuan Di, when Crown Prince Yin was to receive the capping ceremony, an edict ordered Xing Zicai to compose the style name.

sentences.zh: 子才字之曰正道。

translations.literal: Zicai styled him Zhengdao.
translations.idiomatic: Zicai styled him Zhengdao.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「正，一止也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Zheng—one stop.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Zheng—one stop.

sentences.zh: 吾兒其替乎？

translations.literal: Will my son be replaced?
translations.idiomatic: Will my son be replaced?

sentences.zh: 」子才請改，帝不許，曰：「天也。

translations.literal: " Zicai requested a change; the emperor would not permit it, saying: "It is Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: " Zicai requested a change; the emperor would not permit it, saying: "It is Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 」因顧謂常山王演曰：「奪時任汝，慎無殺也。

translations.literal: " He then turned to Prince Changshan Wang Yan and said: "When the time comes I give the throne to you—take care not to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: " He then turned to Prince Changshan Wang Yan and said: "When the time comes I give the throne to you—take care not to kill him.

sentences.zh: 」及帝崩，太子嗣位，常山果廢之而自立。

translations.literal: " When the emperor died, the crown prince succeeded; Changshan indeed deposed him and installed himself.
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor died, the crown prince succeeded; Changshan indeed deposed him and installed himself.

sentences.zh: 殷尋見害。

translations.literal: Yin was soon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was soon killed.

sentences.zh: 武成帝時，左僕射和士開言於帝曰：「自古帝王，盡為灰土，堯舜、桀紂，竟亦何異。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wucheng, Left Vice Director He Shikai said to the emperor: "Since antiquity all emperors and kings have turned to ash—Yao, Shun, Jie, and Zhou—what difference is there in the end?
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wucheng, Left Vice Director He Shikai said to the emperor: "Since antiquity all emperors and kings have turned to ash—Yao, Shun, Jie, and Zhou—what difference is there in the end?

sentences.zh: 陛下宜及少壯，恣意歡樂，一日可以當千年，無為自勤約也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should while still young and strong indulge freely in pleasure—one day can equal a thousand years; do not constrain yourself with diligence and moderation.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should while still young and strong indulge freely in pleasure—one day can equal a thousand years; do not constrain yourself with diligence and moderation.

sentences.zh: 」帝悅其言，彌加淫侈。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased with these words and indulged ever more in licentious extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased with these words and indulged ever more in licentious extravagance.

sentences.zh: 士開既導帝以非道，身又擅權，竟為御史中丞所殺。

translations.literal: Shikai, having led the emperor into the wrong path, also usurped power himself—in the end he was killed by the Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai, having led the emperor into the wrong path, also usurped power himself—in the end he was killed by the Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 武平中，陳人寇彭城，後主發言憂懼，侍中韓長鸞進曰：「縱失河南，猶得為龜茲國子。
